articles.title: Advances in assessment systems and non-pharmacological intervention strategies for cancer-related fatigue following transarterial chemoembolization in hepatocellular carcinoma: a narrative review.
articles.authors: Shiying Yang, Xuelei Yao, Yali Ren, Teng Ding, Jiamin Gao, Lin Shentu
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract: Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) is a primary treatment for intermediate to advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC); however, cancer-related fatigue (CRF) is a prevalent and distressing symptom following TACE that significantly impairs patients' recovery and health-related quality of life. This review aimed to systematically summarize the current evidence on CRF screening, assessment, and non-pharmacological interventions specifically tailored to the post-TACE HCC population, and to propose an integrated, nurse-led clinical management framework. A narrative review was conducted by systematically searching PubMed, Web of Science, and CNKI for literature published up to April 2026. The search encompassed peer-reviewed original research articles (including randomized controlled trials, cohort studies, cross-sectional studies, and meta-analyses), clinical practice guidelines, and expert consensus reports. The level of evidence for each intervention category was evaluated using the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine (OCEBM) grading system. The literature search focused on CRF epidemiology, pathophysiology, validated assessment tools, non-pharmacological interventions (including exercise, psychosocial support, nutritional management, and traditional Chinese medicine therapies), and nursing management models in HCC patients following TACE. CRF following TACE is a multifactorial symptom driven by treatment-induced inflammation, hepatic dysfunction, and psychological distress. Validated screening tools, including the Brief Fatigue Inventory (BFI), Cancer Fatigue Scale (CFS), and EORTC QLQ-C30 fatigue subscale, are recommended for routine use, though to the best of our knowledge, no CRF assessment tool developed specifically for the post-TACE HCC population has been validated to date. A structured screening pathway encompassing baseline assessment, perioperative monitoring, and long-term follow-up was identified as essential for early detection. Among non-pharmacological interventions, individualized exercise prescriptions (aerobic and resistance training) have been most consistently supported across randomised trials and meta-analyses for alleviating CRF, followed by cognitive behavioral therapy, mindfulness-based stress reduction, and nutritional support. Traditional Chinese medicine approaches, including acupoint massage, auricular acupressure, and moxibustion, showed preliminary potential but require further high-quality validation. A nurse-led multidisciplinary care model integrating assessment, individualized intervention planning, and continuous coordination has been proposed as a promising operational framework for CRF management, endorsed by international CRF practice frameworks. Effective management of CRF after TACE requires a comprehensive, evidence-based approach spanning standardized screening, multimodal non-pharmacological interventions, and a nurse-coordinated multidisciplinary care model. Integrating routine CRF assessment into standard TACE clinical pathways and developing TACE-specific assessment tools are priorities for future research and clinical practice.

articles.title: Low CT-derived vertebral attenuation as a prognostic factor in hepatocellular carcinoma patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors.
articles.authors: Shanshan Jiang, Yi Ren, Yuyang Wang, Yi Li, Lianwei Miao, Weiwei Liu, Guofeng Zhou
articles.abstract: Computed tomography (CT)-derived vertebral attenuation has been recognized as an indicator of prognosis for patients undergoing tumor removal, liver transplant, or transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE) therapy, but similar research has not been reported in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). This study aims to explore the prognostic value of CT-derived vertebral attenuation in HCC patients treated with ICIs. This retrospective study included HCC patients who received ICI treatment at Wuhan Union Hospital between July 2020 and March 2024. CT-derived vertebral attenuation was assessed by measuring mean Hounsfield unit (HU) values in the center of the first lumbar vertebra (L1) on non-contrast CT scans. Based on the optimal cutoff value derived from X-tile software, patients were classified into the CT-derived L1 attenuation-low group (≤100 HU) and the CT-derived L1 attenuation-high group (>100 HU). A comparison of the baseline characteristics of the two groups was made, followed by a propensity score matching (PSM) analysis to balance the variables. The objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate (DCR) were calculated for both groups, and Kaplan-Meier survival curves and Cox regression models were used to analyze overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). The cohort consisted of 357 patients, divided into the L1 attenuation-low group (n = 112) and the L1 attenuation-high group (n = 245). Among all patients, 30.0% (107/357) achieved complete or partial response. After PSM analysis, both groups contained 91 patients. The L1 attenuation-low group had shorter OS (hazard ratio [HR], 1.73; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.15-2.60; P = 0.008) and PFS (HR, 1.47; 95% CI, 1.04-2.08; P = 0.030) than the L1 attenuation-high group. CT-derived L1 attenuation can stratify survival risk for HCC patients undergoing ICI treatment.

articles.title: LASSO-based nomogram to predict early treatment failure in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma treated with SBRT, lenvatinib, and tislelizumab.
articles.authors: Yingchun Zhao, Suming Wang, Li He, Xiaoqian Shen, Miaomiao Zhang, Sujing Zhang
articles.abstract: Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) combined with lenvatinib and tislelizumab has shown potential activity in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but early treatment failure (ETF) remains common. We developed an exploratory model to estimate ETF, defined as radiologically confirmed progressive disease (PD) or all-cause death within 6 months after treatment initiation. This single-center retrospective study included advanced HCC patients treated with the triple regimen from June 2021 to June 2024. Baseline clinical, imaging, and hematological variables were analyzed. LASSO regression with 10-fold cross-validation was used for feature selection. Restricted cubic splines assessed linearity, and λ.1se was examined as a sensitivity analysis. A multivariable logistic regression model was presented as a nomogram. Discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA) were evaluated, with 1000-resample bootstrap internal validation repeating the modeling pipeline. Among 118 patients, 33 (27.9%) experienced ETF; 28 had radiologically confirmed PD and 5 died without prior documented PD. At λ.min, LASSO selected maximum tumor diameter, Vp4 portal vein tumor thrombosis (PVTT), baseline systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), ALBI score, and log10-transformed alpha-fetoprotein (AFP). Under λ.1se, four predictors were retained, with SII excluded. The final model had an apparent ROC-AUC of 0.903 and an optimism-corrected ROC-AUC of 0.866. Calibration showed acceptable agreement between predicted and observed risks. DCA suggested net benefit over an exploratory threshold range of approximately 0.10-0.50, which should not be interpreted as a validated treatment-switching threshold. The nomogram showed promising internal discrimination for estimating 6-month ETF risk in advanced HCC patients receiving SBRT, lenvatinib, and tislelizumab. Given the modest sample size and single-center design, the model remains exploratory and hypothesis-generating. External multicenter validation is required before clinical implementation or use for treatment selection.

articles.title: From metastatic disease to no evidence of disease after conversion liver surgery in advanced gastric cancer with liver metastases: A case report.
articles.authors: Dong Chen, Hanyu Wang, Lin Xu
articles.abstract: Stage IV gastric cancer with liver metastases has a poor prognosis. Conversion surgery may enable long-term disease control in selected patients, but pathological complete response is rare and is usually defined only for surgically resected specimens. Here, a 54-year-old female with initially unresectable, HER2-negative, pMMR-by-IHC, EBER-positive gastric cancer and synchronous liver metastases received first-line XELOX plus tislelizumab for 4 cycles. Because of suspected oxaliplatin hypersensitivity, treatment was changed to cisplatin plus capecitabine plus tislelizumab for 3 cycles. After subsequent suspected platinum hypersensitivity, treatment was changed to capecitabine plus tislelizumab for 7 cycles. After 14 cycles, repeat endoscopic biopsy showed no tumor cells. Imaging showed significant regression of liver lesions. After multidisciplinary discussion, the patient underwent conversion liver surgery comprising resection of selected liver lesions and radiofrequency ablation of other liver lesions. R0 status was confirmed only for the resected liver specimens; ablated lesions had no pathological specimen. Histopathological examination of the resected liver specimens showed no residual viable tumor cells, consistent with pathological complete response in the resected liver lesions. The gastric primary was assessed as clinical complete response by endoscopy and biopsy. At last follow-up 1 month after surgery, imaging showed no evidence of disease; long-term outcome remains unknown. This case illustrates that selected patients with advanced gastric cancer and liver metastases may achieve a strong response to tislelizumab-based immunochemotherapy and liver-directed conversion treatment. However, the long-term benefit, the role of omitting gastrectomy, and the significance of FAPI/FDG discordance remain uncertain.

articles.title: Hypoxia-induced GP73 promotes the Warburg effect in hepatocellular carcinoma via HIF-1α.
articles.authors: Mierkamilijiang Abudureheman, Diwen Zhu, Weixin Ren
articles.abstract: Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE)-induced hypoxia is a key driver of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression. This study investigated whether Golgi protein 73 (GP73) drives the Warburg effect and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) via hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) under hypoxia, thereby promoting HCC malignancy. HepG2 cells were exposed to hypoxia (1% O₂). Lentivirus-mediated GP73 overexpression (LV-GP73) and siRNA-mediated HIF-1α knockdown (si-HIF-1α) were established. Four groups were compared: H + LV-NC (negative control), H + LV-GP73, H + LV-GP73 + si-NC, and H + LV-GP73 + si-HIF-1α. Cell proliferation, apoptosis, migration, and invasion were assessed by colony formation, flow cytometry, and Transwell assays. Glycolysis and mitochondrial respiration were evaluated by biochemical kits and Seahorse XFe24 Analyzer. Protein levels were detected by Western blotting. Clinical validation was performed in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from 169 HCC patients who underwent TACE. GP73 overexpression significantly enhanced colony formation, migration, invasion, glucose consumption, lactate production, LDH activity, ATP levels, and extracellular acidification rate, while decreasing apoptosis (P < 0.05). It also showed a decreasing trend in oxygen consumption rate, indicating Warburg effect activation. It also upregulated HIF-1α, glycolytic enzymes (HK2, SLC2A1, LDHA, PGK1), and Vimentin, but downregulated E-cadherin (P < 0.05). Notably, HIF-1α knockdown reversed all these pro-tumorigenic phenotypes, metabolic reprogramming, and molecular changes. Clinical validation further confirmed that PBMCs from TACE-resistant patients exhibited significantly elevated GP73, HIF-1α, and HK2 expression at both mRNA and protein levels (all P < 0.001), consistent with the in vitro findings. Under hypoxia, GP73 promotes the Warburg effect and EMT through HIF-1α stabilization, facilitating HCC progression. The GP73-HIF-1α axis is a critical mediator of TACE resistance and a potential therapeutic target. PBMC-based detection of this pathway may serve as a non-invasive strategy for monitoring TACE resistance risk.

articles.title: Density-Based Simulation of Constant-Current Atomic Force Microscopy Enables Quantitative Non-Planar Molecular Imaging.
articles.authors: Marvin Krenz, Miguel Wiche, Ulrich Koert, Gregor Witte, André Schirmeisen, Daniel Ebeling, Simone Sanna
articles.abstract: High-resolution atomic force microscopy (AFM) with functionalized tips has enabled bond-resolved imaging of molecular structures on surfaces. However, conventional constant-height operation limits the quantitative characterization of nonplanar, bulky, or strongly corrugated adsorbates. Here, we introduce a density-based simulation framework for constant-current AFM (cc-AFM) that unifies tunneling feedback and probe-particle force modeling within a consistent first-principles approach. The method employs the electronic density obtained from density functional theory to generate STM height profiles, which are coupled to probe-particle simulations while considering tip deflection, oscillation averaging, and probe-tip tunneling. We benchmark the approach by using cc-AFM measurements of Hexafluoropentacene on Cu(111) and 2-iodotriphenylene on Ag(111), two systems exhibiting pronounced molecular corrugation and electronic asymmetry. The simulations reproduce the experimentally observed full-molecule contrast, current-dependent image evolution, and subtle bond-level features. By establishing a unified density-driven framework for constant-current AFM, this work enables quantitative three-dimensional structural imaging of complex adsorbates and provides a transferable methodology for interpreting coupled STM/AFM experiments across a wide range of nanoscale systems.

articles.title: Radiotherapy Reprograms CCR8⁺ Regulatory T Cells via REL-NF-κB to Enforce Spatial Immune Exclusion in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
articles.authors: Huanliang Chen, Shuxuan Wang, Bufu Tang, Yanyan Lin, Pan Zhou, Jiaoyang Yang, Qian-Qian Zhao, Zhao-Chong Zeng
articles.abstract: Radiotherapy is increasingly incorporated into the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but adaptive immunosuppressive remodeling of the tumor microenvironment can limit efficacy. We integrated public bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic cohorts with a murine single-cell atlas, paired human radiotherapy specimens, and functional murine studies. High intratumoral regulatory T cell (Treg) infiltration was associated with poor prognosis across two cohorts. Analyses of single cells identified a CCR8⁺ Treg state that was enriched in advanced tumors, exhibited enhanced suppressive features, and was conserved across species. Spatial analyses showed that CCR8⁺ Tregs accumulated in peritumoral regions enriched in myeloid cells and fibrotic stroma, where CD8⁺ T cell infiltration was limited. Hypofractionated radiotherapy expanded suppressive CCR8⁺ Tregs, while radiation enhanced CCL1 secretion by M2-like tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), providing a recruitment signal. Mechanistically, REL knockdown, chromatin immunoprecipitation, and promoter reporter assays demonstrated that radiation activates REL, which directly binds to and transactivates the CCR8 promoter. CCR8 blockade enhanced radiotherapy efficacy, reduced suppressive Treg features, and increased cytotoxic CD8⁺ T cell activity. These findings identify a REL-NF-κB-CCR8 axis as a mediator of immune adaptation following radiotherapy and support combination therapies targeting CCR8 in HCC.

articles.title: Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma: A Review.
articles.authors: Diamantis I Tsilimigras, Ioannis Ntanasis-Stathopoulos, Timothy M Pawlik
articles.abstract: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) is the second most common primary liver malignancy, and incidence is increasing worldwide. Despite advances in multimodal therapy, 5-year overall survival remains approximately 9%, underscoring the urgent need for improved therapeutic strategies and comprehensive understanding of current management approaches. Surgical resection with regional lymphadenectomy remains the cornerstone of curative therapy, with adjuvant capecitabine established as standard of care after resection. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy may be strongly considered for patients with iCCA with high-risk features, including at least 1 of the following: tumor size larger than 5 cm, multifocal disease, vascular invasion, lymph node involvement, and elevated carbohydrate antigen 19-9. For unresectable, liver-confined disease, locoregional therapies, including transarterial chemoembolization, Y-90 radioembolization, hepatic artery infusion pump chemotherapy, thermal ablation, and radiotherapy, may provide meaningful survival benefits. Liver transplant is emerging as a viable option in highly selected patients with very early iCCA or sustained response to neoadjuvant therapy. In advanced disease, chemoimmunotherapy with gemcitabine/cisplatin plus durvalumab or pembrolizumab has become the first-line treatment. Comprehensive molecular profiling identifies actionable targets in 30% to 40% of patients, including FGFR2 fusions/rearrangements, IDH1 variants, and other alterations amenable to targeted therapies approved by the US Food and Drug Administration. The management of iCCA has evolved substantially with neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy for high-risk resectable disease, enhanced locoregional strategies for liver-confined tumors, chemoimmunotherapy as first-line systemic therapy for advanced disease, and precision oncology approaches targeting recurrent molecular alterations. Multidisciplinary evaluation and comprehensive genomic profiling are essential for optimal patient outcomes.

articles.title: The Landmark Series: Perioperative Management of Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
articles.authors: Skylar L Nahi, Adam C Yopp
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with an increasing burden of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease-associated HCC in Western populations. In treating HCC, recurrence after curative-intent therapy remains common, creating a compelling rationale for perioperative systemic therapy. This Landmark Series review examines the pivotal studies that have shaped the surgical and perioperative management of HCC, tracing the evolution from principles of resectability to contemporary adjuvant and neoadjuvant immune-based strategies. The development of perioperative therapy has been defined by both landmark negative trials and emerging evidence of efficacy. The STORM trial demonstrated that sorafenib's activity in advanced HCC did not translate into benefit after resection or ablation. The IMbrave050 trial subsequently demonstrated an early recurrence-free survival advantage with adjuvant atezolizumab plus bevacizumab that was not sustained with longer follow-up evaluation, whereas the KEYNOTE-937 trial failed to demonstrate benefit with adjuvant pembrolizumab. In contrast, early-phase neoadjuvant immune checkpoint inhibitor-based studies have demonstrated feasibility and meaningful pathologic responses, and the CARES-009 trial provided the first randomized phase III evidence of improved event-free survival with a perioperative immune checkpoint inhibitor-antiangiogenic strategy. Perioperative management of HCC is evolving toward an integrated, multidisciplinary treatment paradigm. Although no broadly applicable adjuvant systemic therapy has been established, emerging perioperative strategies provide proof of concept that systemic therapy may improve outcomes for selected patients. Future progress will depend on biomarker-driven patient selection, molecular residual disease assessment, standardized pathologic response criteria, and clinical trials identifying which patients require perioperative therapy and when treatment should be delivered.

articles.title: Newly diagnosed and relapsed follicular lymphoma: EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up.
articles.authors: Marco Ladetto, Natacha Bolaños, Guy Bouguet, Klaus Herfarth, Wolfram Klapper, Sirpa Leppa, Kim Linton, Armando Lopez-Guillermo
articles.abstract: Follicular lymphoma (FL) is the second most common lymphoma subtype in Europe, with a median age at diagnosis of 60-65 years. It is generally considered an indolent disease, and the median overall survival at diagnosis now likely exceeds 20 years. However, considerable heterogeneity exists. Diagnosis requires adequate biopsy material and a specialized hematopathologist. Staging and prognosis rely on positron emission tomography (PET)-computed tomography (CT). Prognostication at diagnosis is based on several validated clinical prognostic scores. Localized disease is usually treated with radiotherapy ± Rituximab. The treatment of disseminated disease includes active surveillance (or in selected cases Rituximab monotherapy) for low-tumor burden patients, and most often immunochemotherapy (or in selected cases chemo-free therapeutic options), ±antibody maintenance in high-tumor burden patients. For relapsed or refractory disease, treatment with Rituximab-Lenalidomide combination ± Tafasitamab or Epcoritamab from the first relapse and single-agent bispecific antibodies, chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy (CAR-T) cells, and Zanubrutinib-Obinutuzumab after second relapse should be prioritized over immunochemotherapy. Given the long natural history and risk of relapse, careful follow-up is an important part of patient management. Patients should be actively involved in decision-making. In this guideline, we present current evidence-based recommendations for diagnosis, staging, treatment, and follow-up.

articles.title: Thermal ablation in posterosuperior liver segments: Is this an indication to laparoscopic approach?
articles.authors: Alessandro Fogliati, Federica Ferraina, Nicola Zarpellon, Cristina Marialuisa Ciulli, Mauro Alessandro Scotti, Alessandra Elvevi, Davide Leni, Fabrizio Romano
articles.abstract: Primary liver tumors such as hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and colorectal cancer liver metastases, can be treated with liver thermal ablation (LTA). Current evidence comparing percutaneous LTA (P-LTA) and laparoscopic LTA (L-LTA) is inconclusive, and data on lesions in the posterosuperior (PS) liver segments are scarce. This study aimed to compare early local recurrence rates between percutaneous and laparoscopic thermal ablation, with a focus on PS liver segments. This single-centre retrospective study included all consecutive patients treated with P-LTA or L-LTA between 2010 and 2024. The primary outcome was early local recurrence (≤ 6 months); secondary outcomes were subgroup analyses of HCC nodules and microwave ablation-treated nodules. The study included 101 nodules in 69 patients. Overall morbidity was higher after L-LTA, whereas chronic liver disease was more common among P-LTA patients. Early local recurrence was significantly lower after L-LTA (7% vs. 25%), and this difference was accentuated in the PS liver segments (4% vs. 33%). Multivariable analysis identified the percutaneous approach and a lesion size > 3 cm as predictors of early local recurrence. L-LTA appears more effective in reducing early local recurrence, particularly in the PS segments, although P-LTA remains less invasive. Prospective multicentre studies are needed to validate these findings.

articles.title: [Hepatic postinterventional imaging : Modality selection, assessment of therapeutic response, recognition, and radiological management of typical complications].
articles.authors: Antonia Dalmer, Hanka Arndt, Lennart Well, Avinash Kambadakone, Isabel Molwitz
articles.abstract: Postprocedural imaging following hepatic interventions is essential for monitoring treatment success and detecting complications. To provide an overview of imaging follow-up after hepatic interventions (transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt [TIPS], percutaneous transhepatic cholangiography and drainage [PTCD], transarterial chemoembolization [TACE], ablation, selective internal radiotherapy [SIRT]), focusing on the selection of imaging modalities, the assessment of treatment success, and the recognition and radiological management of complications. Narrative review based on the current literature of hepatic radiological interventions. The procedure determines the choice of imaging modality. Following TIPS, functional monitoring is primarily performed using duplex ultrasound. PTCD follow-up focuses on drainage placement and bleeding complications. Following TACE and ablation, immediate hypoperfusion of the lesions is to be expected, whereas a temporary increase in size and peripheral enhancement may occur. Following SIRT, a delayed onset of the treatment effect, as detectable by imaging morphology, is characteristic. Bleeding, abscess formation, fistulas, stent occlusions or malfunctions, and tumor recurrences can be treated further using interventional radiology. Knowledge of typical postprocedural imaging findings, as well as common complications and options for radiological treatment of complications, is crucial.

articles.title: Triple-modal visualized radiohydrogel alleviates post-embolization hypoxia via stage-type procedure in hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.authors: Hu Chen, Hongrui Zhang, Xiaoliu Liang, Minglei Teng, Hui Liu, Zhenjie Li, Weilun Song, Yi Lyu
articles.journal: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
articles.abstract: Transarterial radioembolization (TARE) holds significant potential for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but its effectiveness is hindered by radiation resistance from the post-embolization hypoxic microenvironment and challenges in achieving stable local release of radionuclides. Herein, polydopamine (PDA)-coated MnO2 nanoparticles (MnO2@PDA) with a core-shell structure were introduced as the intratumoral hydrogen peroxide nanocatalyst, and 177Lu was anchored in catechol groups on the PDA surface, achieving the stability of radionuclides. And the radionuclide-coordinated nanocatalyst was incorporated into the poly(ethylene oxide) and poly(propylene oxide) thermosensitive hydrogel to formulate an integrated TARE agent (177Lu-MnO2@PDA-Gel), facilitating secondary encapsulation and ensuring intratumoral retention of radionuclides without leakage. Through a three-stage lytic process, 177Lu-MnO2@PDA-Gel produced oxygen by gradually consuming endogenous H2O2. This allowed for post-embolization radiosensitivity and anti-angiogenesis. Furthermore, the release of manganese ions from the embolic hydrogel can serve as an adjuvant to boost intratumoral immune infiltration and improve the efficacy of embolization and internal radiation. Notably, the superiority of SPECT/PAI/MRI triple-modal imaging via 177Lu-MnO2@PDA-Gel enables real-time and dynamic visualization of TARE. Overall, the smart hydrogel demonstrates long-term oxygen generation, stable internal radiation, and tumor microenvironment remodeling, offering a sequential radiosensitization strategy to address TARE refractoriness, thereby presenting significant clinical value for locoregional therapy of HCC.

articles.title: Multiomics, multi-species profiling, and animal validation identify mitoxyperilysis as a conserved therapeutic target in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis.
articles.authors: Hanjie Liu, Cong Qi, Ruixia Lu, Chuan An, Yangzhiyuan Wang, Shumiao Li, Rui Zhu, Xingzhong Feng
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is driven by complex intercellular communication and regulated cell death pathways. Mitoxyperilysis, a recently characterized form of regulated lytic cell death, remains poorly defined in MASH. Here, we integrated multiomics, cross-species transcriptomics, machine learning, and in vivo models to dissect mitoxyperilysis activation and its therapeutic relevance in MASH. Single‑cell and spatial transcriptomic datasets from mouse and human MASH livers were analyzed. Cell-cell communication was inferred using CellChat, and metabolite‑mediated cell-cell communication (mCCC) was assessed with MEBOCOST. Mitoxyperilysis activity was scored via AUCell and AddModuleScore. Eleven machine learning classifiers identified transcriptomic signatures distinguishing MASH from controls, and key regulators were subjected to in silico knockout (scTenifoldKnk). A choline‑deficient, L‑amino acid‑defined high‑fat diet (CDAHFD) mouse model was used for in vivo validation. Single‑cell profiling revealed that mitoxyperilysis activity was highly enriched in myeloid cells, particularly monocyte‑derived macrophages (Mo‑Macrophages) and neutrophils, and was strongly induced by high‑fat high‑sucrose diet. CellChat and mCCC analyses demonstrated that Mo‑Macrophages served as central hubs of rewired inflammatory and metabolic crosstalk in MASH. Spatial transcriptomics confirmed the expansion of pro‑inflammatory hepatocyte subsets and conserved upregulation of mitoxyperilysis components (e.g. BAX, TLR4, NINJ1) in both mouse and human MASH. Cross‑species profiling across mouse, rat, hamster, non‑human primate, and human datasets demonstrated evolutionarily conserved activation of the entire mitoxyperilysis pathway. Machine learning identified Bax as the sole overlapping driver gene linking diet‑induced transcriptomic signatures to mitoxyperilysis. In silico Bax ablation perturbed lipid metabolism and immune pathways. In CDAHFD-induced MASH mice with typical pathological phenotypes, core mitoxyperilysis genes were transcriptionally upregulated, and Bax/Bid/Bak1 upregulation was validated at the protein level. While RhoA mRNA increased, total RhoA protein remained stable, with its ubiquitination elevated and activity suppressed. Mitoxyperilysis is an evolutionarily conserved, myeloid‑enriched pathway activated in MASH. Bax acts as a critical regulatory node, while RhoA is modulated via ubiquitination and functional suppression. Targeting this axis may provide a novel therapeutic strategy for MASH.

articles.title: Network analysis of core symptom changes in hepatocellular carcinoma survivors after transarterial chemoembolization: A longitudinal study.
articles.authors: Suping Wang, Xiuyan Wang, Ni Jiang, Yongpei Hu, Lirong Guo, Long Zhang, Yanzhe Liu, Simin Kong
articles.abstract: The aims of this study were to explore the longitudinal trajectories of core symptoms in survivors with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) after transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) and to analyze their associations with health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and unmet supportive care needs. This longitudinal study enrolled 271 HCC survivors undergoing TACE in China. Patient-reported outcomes were assessed at three time points-24 h (T1), 7 days (T2), and 1 month (T3) post-TACE-using four validated instruments: the MD Anderson Symptom Inventory-Chinese Version (MDASI-C), the Tumor Symptom Measure for Primary Liver Cancer (TSM-PLC), the Quality of Life Instrument for Liver Cancer (QOL-LC V2.0), and the Short Form of Survivors' Unmet Needs Scale (SF-SUNS). Exploratory factor analysis was conducted to extract discrete symptom clusters, and network analysis was used to calculate strength centrality (rs)-an index quantifying the sum of absolute edge weights connecting each symptom to all others-to identify core symptoms. Five symptom clusters were identified at T1: Fatigue-Cognitive, Post-embolization, Somatic, Emotional, and Hepatobiliary-Specific. The Post-embolization cluster was present only at T1, whereas the remaining four clusters persisted at T2 and T3. However, the core symptom shifted over time: nausea at T1 (rs = 1.154), lack of appetite at T2 (rs = 1.229), and sadness at T3 (rs = 1.107). HRQoL was lowest at T1, improved at T2, and declined at T3, with all pairwise comparisons significant (all p < 0.001). Unmet needs were highest at T3, with all time-point differences significant (all p < 0.001). The largest gaps were observed in information provision, care continuity, and emotional support. Greater symptom severity was significantly associated with poorer HRQoL at all time points (all p < 0.01). During the first month post-TACE, the sequence of core symptoms transitioned from nausea to lack of appetite and then to sadness, suggesting time-specific supportive care strategies-including antiemetic prophylaxis, nutritional support, and psychosocial care. Routine assessment of unmet needs may help reduce symptom burden and optimize long-term HRQoL for these survivors.

articles.title: Developing a Better Hepatocellular Carcinoma Treatment: AlEu MOF Nanoparticles Enhance Microwave Thermal Ablation and Synergistically Activate the cGAS-STING Pathway.
articles.authors: Shaoshi Ma, Yingying Wei, Borui Ma, Wenhui Dong, Feng Li, Xiao Li, Lin Chen, Yongzhen Yang
articles.abstract: To address the high recurrence rate of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) following microwave ablation (MWA) therapy, this study develops aluminum-europium metal-organic framework (AlEu MOF) nanoparticles that enhance MWA efficacy by physically improving thermal ablation and activating cyclic GMP-AMP (cGAMP) synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING)-mediated antitumor immunity. AlEu MOF nanoparticles were synthesized via a one-pot hydrothermal method and characterized for physicochemical properties. Biocompatibility and in vitro cell-killing efficacy in combination with MWA were evaluated in Hepa1-6 cell lines. Immunostimulatory capacity was assessed by measuring activation markers of the cGAS-STING pathway. In vivo antitumor efficacy was investigated in a Hepa1-6 subcutaneous tumor-bearing mouse model, with monitoring of tumor growth, intratumoral temperature elevation, serum levels of cGAS-STING pathway downstream effectors, and treatment safety. AlEu MOF nanoparticles demonstrated excellent biocompatibility and hemocompatibility. In combination with MWA, AlEu MOF significantly enhanced thermal efficiency within tumors, resulting in superior tumor growth inhibition compared with MWA alone. Mechanistically, the enhanced thermal ablation triggered mitochondrial damage and downstream cGAS-STING pathway activation, as evidenced by elevated serum levels of key downstream cytokines (IFN-γ, IL-6 and TNF-α) in the combination therapy group. No significant hepatorenal toxicity or major organ damage was observed throughout the treatment period. The AlEu MOF nanoparticles potentiate MWA therapy through a dual synergistic mechanism: enhanced thermal ablation serves as the upstream trigger for cGAS-STING activation, while europium ions simultaneously amplify the STING signaling output, together converting local thermal ablation into systemic antitumor immunity. This synergistic strategy offers a promising approach for enhancing both local tumor ablation and systemic antitumor immunity in HCC.

articles.title: Study protocol of a prospective, non-interventional cohort study evaluating the benefits of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma receiving first-line atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (NISTIPS TRITICC-4, IKF092).
articles.authors: Carolin Angendohr, Christian Weigel, Anselm Kunstein, Markus Joerdens, Thorsten Goetze, Salah-Eddin Al-Batran, Bianca Zäpf, Maria Gonzalez-Carmona
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with most patients diagnosed at an advanced stage. Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab is a current standard first-line therapy; however, outcomes are strongly influenced by underlying cirrhosis and clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH). Complications such as ascites and variceal bleeding may limit treatment continuation, particularly as bevacizumab increases bleeding risk. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) reduces portal pressure and may improve outcomes, but its role in patients receiving immunoncology-based systemic therapy remains unclear. NISTIPS TRITICC-4 is a prospective, multicentre, non-interventional cohort study conducted at up to 25 centers in Germany. A total of 350 adult patients with cirrhosis and unresectable or metastatic HCC receiving first-line atezolizumab plus bevacizumab will be enrolled. Patients are allocated to two cohorts: TIPS in situ plus atezolizumab and bevacizumab or atezolizumab plus bevacizumab alone, according to routine clinical practice.The primary endpoint is time to deterioration of liver function (TTDL), defined as persistent worsening of liver parameters for >4 weeks. Secondary endpoints include overall survival, time on treatment, overall response rate, time to new extrahepatic lesions or death, and safety with focus on bleeding and TIPS-related complications.Time-to-event endpoints will be analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox models. Propensity score matching will be applied to adjust for confounding. Analyses are exploratory. This study will provide real-world evidence on the impact of TIPS in HCC patients receiving atezolizumab plus bevacizumab and may support more individualized management strategies in this high-risk population. www.clinicaltrials.gov identifier is NCT07365930.

articles.title: Combined TIPS and TACE for patients with hepatocellular carcinoma and variceal bleeding secondary to portal vein tumor thrombus.
articles.authors: Zhuyu Feng, Bifei Wu, Zhongwei Xu, Wei Yang, Haifeng Zhou, Haibin Shi, Sheng Liu, Weizhong Zhou
articles.abstract: The study aimed to assess the safety and efficacy of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) combined with transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) for treating hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients who have portal vein tumor thrombus (PVTT) and variceal bleeding secondary to portal hypertension. This retrospective study analysed 39 patients with HCC and PVTT who experienced variceal bleeding and were treated with TIPS and TACE from June 2018 to April 2025. The evaluated outcomes included the technical success, clinical success and overall survival (OS). The technical success rate was 100%. Variceal bleeding was successfully controlled in all patients. Among these patients, 13 (33.3%) developed overt hepatic encephalopathy (HE) after TIPS. There were no other significant procedure-related complications. The recurrence rate of variceal bleeding was 25.6% at 1 year. After TACE, all patients exhibited a reduction in tumor size, with 26 (66.7%) patients achieving partial response (PR) and 13 (33.3%) patients achieving stable disease (SD). The median OS was 12.2 (95% CI: 10.9-13.5) months and OS rates were 89.7% at 1 month, 76.9% at 3 months, 56.4% at 6 months, and 46.2% at 12 months. TIPS combined with TACE appears to be safe and effective for patients who had HCC and PVTT complicated with variceal bleeding secondary to portal hypertension. This study found that the combination of TIPS and TACE is a safe and effective treatment for patients with HCC and PVTT. The treatment successfully stopped the bleeding in all patients, helped shrink the tumors in most, and improved overall survival. This approach not only manages the life-threatening bleeding but also allows for further treatment of the liver cancer itself.

articles.title: CBX4 and NOX4 Expression Are Associated With Chemoradiotherapy Response and Overall Survival in Locally Advanced Cervical Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
articles.authors: Xianfang Pang, Xiyun Qin, Lilin Que, Weiye Li, Zixuan Yang, Weili Yi, Jiao Tang, Yong Zhang
articles.abstract: Tissue biomarkers may improve risk stratification in locally advanced cervical cancer before definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT). We evaluated pretreatment expression of chromobox 4 (CBX4), NADPH oxidase 4 (NOX4), specificity protein 1 (SP1), and copper transporter 1 (CTR1) in relation to CCRT response and overall survival. In this retrospective 1:1 matched case-control study, pretreatment biopsies from 40 patients with locally advanced cervical squamous cell carcinoma (20 CCRT-resistant, 20 CCRT-sensitive) were quantified by AI-assisted digital pathology using H-scores. A parsimonious CBX4 + NOX4 logistic model was evaluated by apparent ROC, leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV), repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation, and bootstrap optimism correction. Overall survival analyses were exploratory. CBX4 and NOX4 expression was lower in CCRT-resistant tumors (median H-score: CBX4, 40.47 vs. 79.62; NOX4, 7.00 vs. 53.93; both p < 0.001), whereas SP1 and CTR1 did not differ. Apparent AUCs were 0.840 for CBX4 and 0.843 for NOX4. The two-marker model had an apparent AUC of 0.903, LOOCV AUC 0.845, repeated 5-fold CV AUC 0.854 ± 0.022, and bootstrap-corrected AUC 0.883. High CBX4 and NOX4 expression was associated with better 5-year overall survival; in joint Cox models, hazard ratios per 1-SD increase were 0.31 (95% CI 0.13-0.74) for CBX4 and 0.48 (0.26-0.90) for NOX4. No histochemically detectable copper deposits were observed. Lower pretreatment CBX4 and NOX4 expression was associated with a CCRT-resistant phenotype and poorer overall survival in this small, response-enriched cohort. Internal resampling suggested discrimination, but same-dataset marker selection may introduce residual optimism and does not establish generalizability. Independent validation in a consecutively recruited cohort is required before clinical application. No mechanisms involving DNA repair, ROS, or chemoradiotherapy sensitivity were established.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence in personalized internal dosimetry for radiopharmaceutical therapy: a narrative mini-review.
articles.authors: Mohammed A Jowhari
articles.abstract: Personalized internal radiation dosimetry supports individualized radiopharmaceutical therapy but remains difficult to implement because workflows require repeated quantitative imaging, segmentation, registration, kinetic modeling, and absorbed-dose calculation. This mini-review summarizes current evidence on artificial intelligence across the personalized dosimetry workflow and considers clinical readiness. A narrative PubMed search was completed in early 2026 and covered peer-reviewed studies published from 2015 to early 2026. Studies addressing artificial intelligence, machine learning, or deep learning in quantitative image reconstruction, segmentation, registration, time-activity curve estimation, absorbed-dose calculation, or clinical decision support were considered. Studies reporting quantitative performance or validation results were prioritized. Deep learning reduced yttrium-90 single-photon emission computed tomography reconstruction error from 149.5% ± 31.2% to 9.2% ± 1.7%; lesion dose-rate error was 8.6% ± 5.7% in virtual-patient testing. Learning-based registration reduced computation time from about 50 s to under 6 s. Single-time-point approaches can simplify imaging, and recent machine learning work has explored prediction of organ effective half-life. Automated segmentation methods show improving reproducibility, whereas evidence for artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support remains mainly retrospective and single-center. Artificial intelligence applications in reconstruction and segmentation appear closer to clinical readiness, while decision-support applications still require prospective, multicenter validation.

articles.title: Multi-omics analysis reveals osteocyte loss as a potential trigger for liver lipid metabolic disorder.
articles.authors: Yuchen Tian, Siyuan Zhu, Chenyi Jiang, Fang Ye, Senyao Zhang, Bingqi Wang, Yiyang Ma, Yidan Pang
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
articles.abstract: Bone regulates whole-body homeostasis via secretory proteins, and clinical observations have suggested potential links between certain skeletal pathologies and liver abnormalities under specific clinical contexts. This study established a postnatal-specific osteocyte knockout mouse model (Dmp1cre DTRfl/fl). Livers were collected for Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), bulk transcriptomic analysis, and metabolomic analysis to reveal the impact of osteocytes ablation on liver metabolism. Multi-omics analysis revealed alterations in lipid metabolism, with upregulation of Cyp4a10 related to oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation, and downregulation of Scd1 involved in fatty acid biosynthesis. scRNA-seq identified changes in gene expression patterns in hepatocytes, endothelial cells, and Kupffer cells, with key transcription factors (Yy1 in hepatocytes and Etv5 in endothelial cells) associated with steatosis. Altered cellular communication networks, particularly the Grn-sort1 and Angptl4-Sdc axes, potentially reshaped liver metabolism and facilitated steatosis in Dmp1cre DTRfl/fl mice. Histological analysis confirmed the development of hepatic steatosis in Dmp1cre DTRfl/fl mice. Loss of osteocytes has potential role in liver lipid metabolic disturbances and fat accumulation, mediated through the modulation of lipid and inflammatory gene expression and alterations in intra-cellular communication within the liver. These findings enhance our understanding of how bone disease can initiate systemic metabolic disorders and provide support for the concept of the bone-liver axis.

articles.title: Cost Analysis of Percutaneous Segmentectomy Versus Chemoembolisation and Radioembolisation in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Retrospective Multicentre Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Pierleone Lucatelli, Laura Crocetti, Renato Argirò, Roberto Iezzi, Chiara Reale, Valeria Grillo, Tetyana Shchipska, Alessandro Maresca
articles.abstract: To compare the costs of percutaneous segmentectomy, a single-session combination of transarterial embolisation and microwave ablation, against chemoembolisation and radioembolisation for hepatocellular carcinoma. Retrospective cost analysis of 66 patients treated with percutaneous segmentectomy at five Italian centres, using bottom-up micro-costing. Comparator costs were derived from published Italian per-session costs multiplied by mean sessions per patient, and survival from published curves. A partitioned survival model estimated life-years and incremental net monetary benefit at 50,000 euros per life-year. Procedural cost per treated patient was 6331 euros for percutaneous segmentectomy, 9792 euros for chemoembolisation (mean 2.94 sessions), and 21,673 euros for radioembolisation (1.52 sessions). At 24 months, percutaneous segmentectomy had lower total cost and a small life-year deficit (incremental cost-effectiveness ratio approximately 70,800 euros per life-year versus chemoembolisation and 57,500 versus radioembolisation, both above threshold). This life-year-adjusted advantage reversed versus chemoembolisation, and became neutral versus radioembolisation, in a worst-case sensitivity analysis, and reversed against both when transplantation costs for the eight transplanted patients (19%) were attributed to percutaneous segmentectomy alone. In this exploratory analysis, percutaneous segmentectomy appeared to have a lower procedural cost per treated patient than chemoembolisation and radioembolisation, mainly because it is delivered in a single session. However, because costing routes, cohorts, and survival sources were not equivalent and the life-year-adjusted comparison was not robust, no formal cost superiority can be established. These hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in prospective, matched studies. Level 4, Retrospective Cohort Study with Historical Comparators.

articles.title: Distinct migratory dendritic cell subsets cooperate to prime tissue-resident memory-like CD8⁺ T cells in mouse tumors.
articles.authors: Nathan Vaudiau, Pierre Bourdely, Maria Semitekolou, Agathe Ok, Louise Gorline, Aboubacar Sidiki K Coulibaly, Matthieu Rastello, Aurélie Semervil
articles.abstract: Tumor-infiltrating tissue-resident memory (TRM)-like CD8+ T cells correlate with positive prognosis and better responses to cancer immunotherapy, yet the mechanisms underlying their specification remain ill-understood. Here, we use the KP (KrasG12D, p53-/-) mouse model of lung adenocarcinoma to investigate how different dendritic cell (DC) subsets shape tumor-specific CD8+ T cell responses. Selective ablation of XCR1+ DC1s or IRF4-dependent CD11b+ DC2s reveal that DC1s, but not DC2s, are required for the generation of tumor-infiltrating effector and exhausted CD8+ T cells. By contrast, both migratory DC1s and migratory DC2s contribute to the specification of CD103+CD69+ TRM-like CD8+ T cells in tumor-draining lymph nodes. Mechanistically, low peptide/MHC-I density on migratory DC2s favors TGFβ-dependent TRM differentiation, while high peptide/MHC-I density on DC1s promote proliferative expansion of TRM-like cells; in addition, IL-12 secreted by DC1s enhances CXCR6 expression. Together, our findings uncover complementary functions of migratory DC subsets in shaping anti-tumor TRM-like CD8+ T cell responses, and also implicate targeting multiple DC subsets for optimizing cancer immunotherapy.

articles.title: A deep learning framework for threshold-free relative gene expression ranking from histone modification signals.
articles.authors: Abdul Munif, Amitava Datta, Zhaoyu Li, Max Ward
articles.abstract: Current methods for predicting gene expression from histone modifications rely on arbitrary binary classification thresholds such as the median to distinguish between high and low expression for genes. This approach lacks biological justification, creates dataset-dependent classifications, and ignores the relative regulatory relationships between genes that are often more biologically meaningful than absolute cutoffs. We developed a deep learning method using pairwise ranking to determine the relative gene expression levels between gene pairs based on their histone modification signals. The approach adopted the DirectRanker architecture, which enforces antisymmetry by construction through a twin-subnet design with asymmetric subtraction, and was evaluated against three baseline classifiers (Random Forest, Logistic Regression, and SVM Linear) on identical features and data splits. Ablation testing across all 31 non-empty subsets of five histone marks (H3K4me3, H3K9ac, H3K9me3, H3K27ac, H3K27me3) was conducted to identify their individual contributions. Datasets were strictly partitioned (80% training, 10% validation, 10% testing) with gene-level separation to prevent data leakage, and all experiments were repeated across five independent random seeds. Four datasets were analysed: two normal adult liver cell datasets (Donor 3 and Donor 4 from NCBI GEO GSE19465) and two HepG2 hepatocellular carcinoma cell line datasets (ENCSR134DWG and GSE76344). Multi-mark combinations anchored by active histone marks (H3K27ac, H3K4me3, H3K9ac) consistently drove predictive performance, with the best combinations achieving AUROC values of 0.833-0.867 and test accuracies of 74-78% across datasets. DirectRanker attained AUPRC values of 0.819-0.856, closely matching or exceeding Random Forest on precision-recall performance. Repressive marks (H3K9me3, H3K27me3) consistently underperformed when used in isolation, with single-mark models achieving test accuracies of only 50-66%. DirectRanker produced substantially higher antisymmetry scores (0.961-0.983) than all baseline classifiers (0.787-0.851), confirming logically consistent pairwise predictions. Performance plateaued at four- to five-mark combinations, reflecting correlated predictive signal among the active marks within the promoter-proximal feature space. The pairwise ranking framework provides a principled alternative to threshold-based classification, enabling relative gene expression comparisons without arbitrary binarisation cutoffs. While Random Forest achieved marginally higher accuracy, DirectRanker's structural antisymmetry guarantee makes it the more suitable choice for applications requiring a globally coherent gene ranking. Active promoter marks carry the majority of the predictive signal, while the performance saturation with increasing mark combinations reflects overlapping information content rather than biological redundancy.

articles.title: Preoperative HAIC enlarges future liver remnant in initial unresectable HCC patients with Vp3 tumor thrombus.
articles.authors: Yifan Zhang, Yiquan Lu, Yuchen Yang, Xinyi Luo, Nan Wang, Fengjie Hao, Weixia Li, Yongjun Chen
articles.abstract: Conversion strategy is the optimal treatment for patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC). However, a severe lack of future liver remnant (FLR) may result in early withdrawal. In this small sample retrospective study, we investigated FLR changes after conversion therapies. Notably, patients with ipsilateral Vp3 portal vein tumor thrombus (PVTT) showed a significant FLR increase after treatment and provided an advantage for carrying out radical surgery. 53 uHCC patients with Vp0 to Vp3 tumor thrombus were enrolled and divided into two groups (Vp0-2 and Vp3) based on the initial PVTT status. All patients received anti-PD-L1 and anti-VEGF therapy combined with hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC) every three weeks. The FLR was measured at baseline and after 3-4 cycles. The odds ratio (OR) between Vp3 and FLR changes was calculated. Among the 53 patients, 28 achieved complete response (CR) or partial response (PR) after conversion treatment. FLR did not change in Vp0-2 group, regardless of the response. While a significant FLR increase was observed in Vp3 group, especially in patients with CR and PR. 10 cases of successfully converted Vp3 patients showed an average FLR enlargement of 18.5%. According to our study, Vp3 patients demonstrated greater FLR enlargement after conversion therapy combined with HAIC, probably due to the thrombus' restriction on blood flow to the tumor side liver. This observation may help to increase both the surgeons' and the uHCC patients' confidence in continuing treatment.

articles.title: Sequential transarterial radioembolization and atezolizumab plus bevacizumab improves survival in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.authors: Yunmi Ko, Hyunjae Shin, Moon Haeng Hur, Jeayeon Park, Jin Woo Choi, Yun Bin Lee, Eun Ju Cho, Jeong-Hoon Lee
articles.abstract: Yttrium-90 transarterial radioembolization (TARE) combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors has been investigated as a potential therapeutic strategy for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC); however, evidence supporting its addition to current standard systemic therapy remains limited. We aimed to compare clinical outcomes in patients with advanced HCC treated with TARE followed by atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (TARE-Atezo/Bev) and Atezo/Bev alone. This retrospective cohort study included systemic therapy-naïve patients with advanced HCC treated with Atezo/Bev alone or TARE-Atezo/Bev at a single tertiary hospital between 2018 and 2025. Baseline characteristics were adjusted using propensity score matching (PSM) and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). The primary outcome was overall survival (OS), and the secondary outcome was progression-free survival (PFS). A total of 156 eligible patients were enrolled, including 93 in the Atezo/Bev group and 63 in the TARE-Atezo/Bev group. In the unmatched cohort, median OS was significantly longer in the TARE-Atezo/Bev group than in the Atezo/Bev group (14.1 vs 6.4 months; hazard ratio=0.43, 95% confidence interval = 0.29-0.63; p < 0.001), with consistent results after PSM (p = 0.01) and IPTW (p < 0.001). Although PFS was comparable between groups in the overall cohort, patients with Child-Pugh class A (OS: 14.6 vs 7.1 months; PFS: 7.7 vs 6.3 months) or ALBI grade 1 (OS: 21.4 vs 8.3 months; PFS: 8.1 vs 5.7 months) had significantly longer OS and PFS in the TARE-Atezo/Bev group, with similar results after adjustment. Sequential TARE-Atezo/Bev may improve survival compared with Atezo/Bev alone in patients with advanced HCC and well-preserved liver function. QuestionThe survival benefit of yttrium-90 TARE followed by Atezo/Bev compared with Atezo/Bev alone remains uncertain given limited evidence in advanced HCC. FindingsTARE followed by Atezo/Bev was associated with significantly longer OS than Atezo/Bev alone, with both OS and PFS improved in patients with advanced HCC and preserved liver function. Clinical relevanceSequential TARE followed by Atezo/Bev may offer a survival advantage in selected patients with advanced HCC, supporting the integration of locoregional and systemic therapies.

articles.title: Treatment patterns and outcomes in US patients with unresectable HCC treated with embolization.
articles.authors: Kirema Garcia-Reyes, William H Wang, Mufiza Farid-Kapadia, Nehemiah Kebede, Dex L Underwood, Ling Cai, Heide A Stirnadel-Farrant, Cindy Wang
articles.abstract: To describe treatment patterns and outcomes in patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC) treated with embolization. This retrospective observational study used Optum's de-identified Market Clarity Data. US adults with HCC treated with embolization between July 2016-September 2022 were followed from first embolization following diagnosis until death and end of enrollment or study period. Of 1,458 patients, 41.9%, 33.5%, and 24.6% received transarterial radioembolization (TARE), transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), and transarterial embolization (TAE), respectively, as initial embolization therapy; TARE use increased over time. Most were male (74.6%), white (66.5%), with a median age at index of 65.0 years, and 63.1% required ≥1 subsequent treatment (median treatment pattern follow-up: 16.3 months). Median (95% CI) time to first follow-up treatment or death was 5.9 (5.5-6.4) months. Compared with TARE, risk of death was lower with TACE (HR [95% CI] 0.82 [0.69-0.97]; P = 0.0242], non-significant in missingness sensitivity analysis) and higher with TAE (HR [95% CI] 1.25 [1.05-1.49]; P = 0.0135]). TARE was the most common initial embolization therapy and its use increased over time. Time to first follow-up treatment or death was relatively short. Future studies are needed to identify optimal treatment approaches.

articles.title: Three traditional Chinese patent medicines combined with transarterial chemoembolization for primary liver cancer: A systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Wei Jiang, Jun Luo, Chenguang Wu, Yan An, Yinzhong Dai, Junwei Shi, Chengying Lan, Jinfeng Qi
articles.abstract: To evaluate the objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate of 3 Chinese herbal medicines (Compound Banmao Capsule, Huaier Granule, and Jinlong Capsule) combined with transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) for primary liver cancer using Bayesian network meta-analysis. We systematically searched randomized controlled trials (RCTs) across the Cochrane Library, Embase, PubMed, Web of Science, VIP Database for Chinese Technical Periodicals, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang databases from their inception to January 10, 2025. Two researchers independently screened the literature, extracted data, and assessed study quality using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. A Bayesian network meta-analysis was performed using RStudio to synthesize and hierarchically rank interventions by effect size in the included RCTs. This review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251019361). Thirty-one RCTs involving 2604 patients with primary liver cancer were included. The network meta-analysis showed that, compared with TACE alone: Compound Banmao Capsule ranked highest for ORR (OR = 1.50, 95% CI: 1.08, 2.08), followed by Huaier Granule (OR = 1.47, 95% CI: 1.05, 2.05) and Jinlong Capsule (OR = 1.30, 95% CI: 1.02, 1.65). For disease control rate, the ranking was Compound Banmao Capsule (OR = 1.21, 95% CI: 0.76, 1.93), Jinlong Capsule (OR = 1.17, 95% CI: 0.85, 1.59), and Huaier Granule (OR = 1.12, 95% CI: 0.66, 1.91). For ORR, the combination of the 3 Chinese herbal medicines with TACE showed superior efficacy to TACE monotherapy, with Compound Banmao Capsule demonstrating the greatest therapeutic potential among the interventions evaluated.

articles.title: TACE-HAIC combined with apatinib and camrelizumab for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma with portal vein tumor thrombus: a multicenter retrospective study.
articles.authors: Xuexian Zhang, Shangbo Shi, Yang Su, Yuanjin Ma, Qikun Guo, Xuerou Meng, Ruidong Wang, Jian Long
articles.abstract: Unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC) with portal vein tumor thrombus (PVTT) indicates a poor prognosis. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) combined with hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC), apatinib, and camrelizumab in patients with uHCC accompanied by PVTT. This multicenter retrospective study included patients with uHCC and PVTT who were treated at five tertiary medical centers in China between December 2021 and April 2025. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to minimize potential confounding bias. Treatment efficacy was assessed by objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS). The primary endpoints were PFS and OS, whereas secondary endpoints included ORR and safety. Among the 222 patients who met the eligibility criteria, 105 received TACE-HAIC combined with apatinib and camrelizumab (THAC group), and 117 received TACE combined with apatinib and camrelizumab (TAC group). After PSM, 86 matched patients were included in each group, and baseline characteristics were well balanced between the two groups. The THAC group achieved significantly higher intrahepatic tumor ORR (70.9% vs. 47.7%, P = 0.002) and DCR (94.2% vs. 79.1%, P = 0.004) than the TAC group. Similarly, for PVTT, the THAC group demonstrated significantly higher ORR (61.6% vs. 41.9%, P = 0.009) and DCR (90.7% vs. 74.4%, P = 0.005). The median PFS was significantly longer in the THAC group than in the TAC group (12 months vs. 7 months; HR = 0.287; 95%CI: 0.204-0.403; P<0.001). Likewise, the median OS was significantly prolonged in the THAC group (24 months vs. 16 months; HR = 0.198; 95%CI: 0.135-0.291; P<0.001). The incidence of adverse events did not differ significantly between the two groups (P>0.05). All adverse events were manageable, and no grade 5 adverse events were observed. In patients with uHCC accompanied by PVTT, the THAC regimen was associated with superior survival outcomes compared with the TAC regimen while maintaining an acceptable safety profile. These findings suggest that THAC may represent a feasible and effective therapeutic option for this patient population.

articles.title: Retrospective observational study of transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE) combined with PD-1 inhibitor and tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.authors: Guohui Xu, Jianlong Zhang, Xiaojun Li, Shilan Fan, Xiao Wu, Cuncai Zhou
articles.abstract: Transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE) induces tumor necrosis and antigen release, but the resulting hypoxic microenvironment upregulates programmed death-ligand 1and vascular endothelial growth factor, providing a biological rationale for adding a programmed death-1 (PD-1) inhibitor and a TKI. The study aims to assess the effectiveness and safety of a treatment regimen consisting of TACE, tyrosine kinase inhibitors, and PD-1 inhibitors in patients diagnosed with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) that cannot be treated surgically. This retrospective observational study (Jiangxi Cancer Hospital, Jan 2021-Jun 2023) enrolled 52 advanced HCC patients, with 45 included in final analysis. Primary endpoints were progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS); secondary endpoints covered objective response rate, Disease Association for the Study of the Liver and safety. Survival was analyzed via Kaplan-Meier method and Cox proportional hazards regression. The cohort comprised 38 men and 7 women with a mean age of 50.9 ± 12.06 years, and 36 patients (80.0%) were hepatitis B virus antigen positive. At 6 months, the PFS rate stood at 71.1%, while at twelve months, it was recorded at 51.7%. The median PFS reached 12.4 months (95% confidence interval: 9.8-15.0), while the median OS was found to be 24.2 months (95% confidence interval: 20.1-28.3). The objective response rate was 44.4% and Disease Association for the Study of the Liver was 91.1%. Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) staging significantly affected prognosis, with median PFS for BCLC A, B, C, and D being 19.2, 16.5, 12.1, and 4.8 months, respectively (log-rank P = .016). Median PFS for first-, second-, and third-line treatments were 17.1, 12.6, and 3.2 months, respectively (log-rank P < .001). Patients with positive node expression had significantly shorter PFS (5.1 vs 9.9 months, HR = 2.89, P = .005) and OS (14.9 vs 25.0 months, HR = 3.24, P = .002) compared to those with negative node expression. No grade 5 adverse events occurred. TACE combined with tyrosine kinase inhibitor and PD-1inhibitors shows promising efficacy and acceptable safety for advanced HCC. BCLC staging, treatment line and node status significantly affect outcomes, with earlier intervention yielding greater survival benefit. These exploratory findings from a small retrospective single-arm study require confirmation in larger prospective trials.

articles.title: Balloon-Occlusion Versus End-Hole Transarterial Chemoembolization for Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Salvatore Tumolo, Afonso Quelhas Fonseca, Vincenzo Vingiani, Tiago Bilhim, Hüseyin Saygin Tuna
articles.abstract: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of balloon-occluded transarterial chemoembolization (B-TACE) compared with conventional (cTACE) and drug-eluting-bead transarterial chemoembolization (DEB-TACE) in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma. A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO. PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched to 8 February 2026 for randomized and observational studies comparing B-TACE with cTACE or DEB-TACE. Tumor response (mRECIST), overall survival, and adverse events were pooled using random-effects models; risk of bias was assessed with established tools. Nine studies (one randomized, eight observational; 1534 patients) were included. Complete response, objective response, disease control, and progressive disease did not differ significantly between groups, with moderate-to-substantial heterogeneity. Baseline tumors were larger in the balloon-occluded group (mean difference 4.34 mm; 95% CI 1.18- 7.50; p = 0.014). Exploratory study-level analyses suggested greater relative B-TACE effects with larger tumors, particularly for complete response and disease control.Overall survival favored B-TACE in the two studies with extractable hazard ratios (HR 0.41; 95% CI 0.23 to 0.73; p = 0.002). Post-treatment liver enzymes, bilirubin, fever, and post-embolization syndrome did not differ significantly. No statistically significant differences in imaging response or safety were observed between intervention and comparator groups, while B-TACE was associated with a signal toward improved overall survival despite larger baseline tumors. Exploratory findings suggested that larger tumor size may be associated with a greater relative B-TACE effect. Given the limited evidence, these findings require confirmation in randomized controlled trials.

articles.title: Adjuvant and Perioperative Systemic Therapy for Resectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Evidence, Biological Rationale, and Trial Design.
articles.authors: Xin Xin, Ruoyu Miao
articles.abstract: Recurrence after curative-intent resection or ablation remains a major barrier to cure in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Postoperative sorafenib was neutral in STORM, the initial recurrence-free survival signal with atezolizumab plus bevacizumab in IMbrave050 was not sustained with longer follow-up, and pembrolizumab was neutral in KEYNOTE-937. By contrast, perioperative camrelizumab plus rivoceranib improved event-free survival in CARES-009. This focused narrative review separates direct HCC clinical evidence from preclinical, cross-tumor, and translational evidence and addresses three development questions: how to test the intact-tumor antigen-source hypothesis, how to select patients biologically, and how to advance perioperative regimens without compromising curative surgery. The primary tumor and its draining lymphatic network may support antigen presentation and expansion of tumor-reactive lymphocytes during checkpoint blockade, but no randomized HCC trial has isolated treatment timing while holding regimen, exposure, population, and time origin constant. CARES-009 therefore validates one complete perioperative strategy rather than proving that neoadjuvant exposure caused benefit. Biological selection should proceed across the treatment pathway: pretreatment clinical risk and liver reserve establish eligibility; on-treatment safety and tissue response assess pharmacodynamic activity; and postoperative pathology, circulating tumor DNA, alpha-fetoprotein/des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin kinetics, and spatial immune features refine residual risk. These markers are prognostic, but none has demonstrated treatment-predictive utility in a randomized biomarker-guided trial. A stage-gated development program should establish agent-specific dose and washout, preserve operability, separate timing and treatment components in randomized phase II studies, and then confirm durable event-free and overall survival in globally representative phase III trials. Durable cure without loss of surgical opportunity, hepatic reserve, or quality of life should define success.

articles.title: Interpretable CT-Based Radiomics for Prediction of High-Affinity Neoantigens Associated Immunogenic States in Advanced Hepatocellular Carcinoma Treated with TACE Plus Targeted Therapy and Immunotherapy.
articles.authors: Chaofan Bian, Yanjin Qin, Hongliang Zou, Wenzhe Fan, Jiaping Li
articles.abstract: Objectives: To develop and validate a CT radiomics-based machine learning model for the noninvasive prediction of HANS status in advanced HCC and to investigate the prognostic and genomic characteristics associated with HANS status. Materials and Methods: This retrospective study included patients with advanced HCC treated with TACE-based triplet therapy. Patients were followed until death or last follow-up. Tumor tissue underwent whole-exome sequencing for HANS calculation, and arterial-phase CT images were used for radiomic feature extraction. A radiomics model (HANS-Rad), a clinical model (HANS-Clin), and a combined model (HANS-RC) were developed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. Calibration and decision curve analyses were performed to assess model reliability and clinical utility. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) were used for model interpretation. Genomic analyses were conducted to explore differences between predicted HANS subgroups. Results: A total of 129 patients were included (median age, 54 years; IQR, 44-62 years; 90% men). The HANS-High group demonstrated longer overall survival compared with the HANS-Low group (median, 23.0 vs. 10.0 months; hazard ratio, 0.60; p = 0.026). The combined HANS-RC model achieved the best performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.964 in the training set and 0.869 (95% CI, 0.716-1.000) in the test set, outperforming the radiomics-only and clinical models. The model also showed favorable calibration and net benefit. Genomic analyses revealed that HANS-High tumors exhibited higher tumor mutational burden and enrichment of immune-related and oncogenic pathways, whereas HANS-Low tumors were associated with distinct mutational patterns and pathway alterations. Conclusions: A radiomics-based machine learning model using CT images enables the noninvasive prediction of HANS status in advanced HCC, with strong prognostic relevance and biologic interpretability supported by genomic analyses.

articles.title: Long-Term Outcomes of Interventional Treatments for Lung Cancer Liver Metastases: Transarterial Chemoembolization and Microwave Ablation.
articles.authors: Thomas J Vogl, Angeliki M Angelopoulou, Tatjana Gruber-Rouh, Catharina Recoschewitz, Hamzah Adwan
articles.abstract: Purpose: The aim of this study was to evaluate the long-term results of transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) and microwave ablation (MWA) as locoregional interventional treatments for lung cancer liver metastases (LCLM) in different protocols and settings. Material and Methods: A total of 56 patients (31 males and 25 females; mean age 59.1 ± 9.8 years) with LCLM were included in our retrospective study, conducted at our department between 2009 and 2024. These patients had undergone different therapies and were divided into two groups depending on the treatment protocol. Twenty-six patients (13 women and 13 men; mean age: 56.8 ± 11.7 years) with 49 tumors were solely treated by TACE, who underwent 77 sessions. A total of thirty patients (18 males and 12 females; mean age 61.2 ± 7.3 years) with 48 tumors were in the ablation-based group (TACE + MWA or MWA-only), who underwent 94 TACE and 53 MWA treatment sessions. Results: The ablation-based group exhibited significantly longer overall survival than the TACE-only group, achieving a median Overall Survival (mOS) of 1.6 years (95% CI: 1.1-2.1) versus 0.5 years (95% CI: 0.2-0.9) for the TACE-only group (Log-Rank χ2 = 12.17, p < 0.001). The survival rates at 1-, 3-, and 5-years were 70%, 23% and 8% for the ablation group, respectively, compared to 20%, 10%, and 0% for the TACE monotherapy group, in which no patient survived beyond 4.5 years. In a multivariable Cox model adjusted for histological subtype, number of lesions, and maximum lesion diameter, TACE monotherapy remained independently associated with mortality (hazard ratio [HR]: 2.711, 95% CI: 1.363-5.391, p = 0.004). With respect to neoadjuvant chemosensitivity, a per-lesion analysis revealed no statistically significant difference in tumor downsizing between Gemcitabine-based (12.6%) and Irinotecan-based (19.7%) regimens (p = 0.452). No major procedure-related complications or treatment-related deaths were identified in the available records across 224 treatment sessions. Conclusions: The ablation-based cohort exhibited significantly longer overall survival than the TACE monotherapy group, and the treatment group remained independently associated with survival after adjustment. Because treatment allocation followed hepatic tumor burden rather than randomization, this association is subject to confounding by indication and is interpreted accordingly. TACE was effective as a neoadjuvant downsizing modality with either chemotherapeutic combination, although the two were applied in different periods and were therefore not compared under equivalent conditions. These findings support the further evaluation of ablation-containing treatment strategies in appropriately selected patients and require confirmation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: A Contemporary Review of Resectability and Treatment Strategies for Colorectal Liver Metastases: Part 2-Advanced Surgical Techniques, Conversion Strategies, and the Expanding Boundaries of Treatment.
articles.authors: Jennifer A Kalil, René Adam, Nicholas Meti, Peter Metrakos
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Most patients with colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) present with disease beyond upfront technical resectability. Advances in systemic therapy, surgical technique, and liver-directed therapies have expanded the proportion of patients who can achieve curative-intent treatment, yet substantial heterogeneity in practice persists. This review provides a structured synthesis of current management strategies for borderline resectable, initially unresectable, and never resectable CRLM. Methods: A structured literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus and the Cochrane Library was performed to identify studies published between 2000 and 2026 using the eligibility criteria described in Part 1 of this review. Findings were synthesized narratively across systemic, surgical, and liver-directed treatment strategies. Results: Future liver remnant augmentation through regenerative procedures offers higher rates of conversion to resection in borderline cases. Conversion chemotherapy enables secondary resection in 12-35% of initially unresectable patients, with regimen selection guided by RAS/BRAF status, primary tumor sidedness, and performance status; however, most pivotal trials were designed for the broader metastatic colorectal cancer population, with conversion to resection rarely serving as the primary endpoint. For never resectable liver-only disease, liver transplantation demonstrates survival advantage in highly selected patients and iterative local therapy remains an area of active investigation. Across all settings, achieving complete local treatment remains the strongest determinant of long-term survival. Conclusions: Management of complex CRLM requires individualized, multidisciplinary decision-making with repeated reassessment of resectability throughout treatment. The evidence is constrained by heterogeneous resectability definitions, reliance on trials not designed for CRLM-specific endpoints, and limited data on several emerging strategies. Standardized eligibility frameworks and CRLM-specific trial designs are needed to advance the field.
