articles.title: Dynamic Multi-Phase-Fused Photon-Counting CT for Pre-TACE Feeding Artery Mapping and DSA Procedural Road-Mapping in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
articles.authors: Hao Chen, Hao Deng, Xin Wei, Xi Liu, Weijuan Chen
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Accurate preoperative feeding artery mapping remains challenging for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) even with modern CT techniques. This study aimed to optimize dynamic multi-phase photon-counting CT (PCCT) hepatic artery protocols and assess dynamic-fusion PCCT against best single-phase PCCT and energy-integrating-detector dual-energy CT (EID-DECT) for feeding artery detection, vascular-map construction and digital subtraction angiography (DSA) path-planning prior to transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) in HCC. Methods: This prospective single-center study contained workflow-optimization among cirrhotic non-HCC patients and clinical validation in TACE-candidate HCC patients. Two radiologists performed blinded independent reading. The composite reference standard consisted of DSA, selective/superselective angiography, available cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and embolization records. Primary endpoint: patient-level paired difference in DSA-verified feeding artery coverage. Secondary endpoints included complete-atlas rate, DSA-path-prediction accuracy, missed-vessel count and extrahepatic-supply detection. A pre-specified comparison between dynamic-fusion PCCT and EID-DECT was performed. Results: Dynamic phase 1-6 fusion was the optimal PCCT scheme, while optimal single-phase varied individually. Dynamic-fusion PCCT achieved superior feeding artery coverage (97.78% ± 8.61% vs. 88.33% ± 15.37%, difference 9.44 pp, 95% CI 1.82-17.06, p = 0.016), complete-atlas rate (93.3% vs. 53.3%, p = 0.039) and path-prediction accuracy (96.67% ± 11.18% vs. 80.00% ± 24.49%), with fewer missed culprit vessels. Two extrahepatic feeders were only detected by dynamic-fusion PCCT. Compared with EID-DECT, dynamic-fusion PCCT showed favorable atlas-related metrics without statistically significant difference in feeding artery coverage. It delivers comprehensive preoperative vascular data and may reduce intraoperative exploratory procedures.

articles.title: Thrombosed Giant Multifocal Hepatic Cavernous Hemangioma Mimicking Lymphatic Malformation on Coaxial Biopsy in an Adult with Recurrent Fever: A Case Report and Focused Literature Review.
articles.authors: Hao Cheng, Jiaxi Ma, Jinghang Xu, Li Liang, Ke Wang, Guiqiang Wang, Na Huo, Yan Wang
articles.abstract: Hepatic cavernous hemangioma is the most common benign liver tumor, but giant or extensively thrombosed variants may lose their characteristic imaging features and mimic other cystic or vascular lesions. A 32-year-old man presented with recurrent fever for more than two months, massive hepatomegaly, leukocytosis (white blood cell count 14.46 × 109/L), C-reactive protein 165.30 mg/L, and greatly elevated D-dimer (48.44 mg/L) and fibrin degradation products (323.52 mg/L), with normal platelet count, fibrinogen, prothrombin time, and activated partial thromboplastin time. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated multiple bilateral cystic or cystic-solid hepatic lesions with calcifications and no classic blood-pool enhancement pattern. 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron-emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) showed no significant uptake, and an extensive microbiological workup was negative. Ultrasound-guided percutaneous biopsy (coaxial technique, 15-gauge needle, five cores from the solid component of the largest right-lobe lesion) favored a benign vascular/lymphatic tumor most consistent with hepatic lymphatic malformation (LM). Subsequently, the patient underwent staged laparoscopic partial hepatectomy combined with microwave ablation at another hospital. The resection pathology demonstrated cystically dilated, blood-filled channels with organizing thrombi, infarction, cholesterol granulomas, and calcification, diagnostic of hepatic cavernous hemangioma with thrombus formation-discordant with the biopsy interpretation. The patient has remained afebrile since surgery, with normalization of inflammatory markers and a fall in D-dimer to 6.95 mg/L. Extensive thrombosis, fibrosis, and calcification can abolish the classic imaging and histopathological features of hepatic hemangioma and make it resemble a lymphatic malformation on coaxial biopsy.

articles.title: MAP2-mediated integrin dysregulation reprograms cancer cell plasticity in hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.authors: Ut Kei Lou, Tin-Lok Wong, Ianto Bosheng Huang, Ka-Hei Lam, Huajian Yu, Ki-Fong Man, Jia Jian Loh, Lei Zhou
articles.abstract: Targeting tumor cell plasticity is central to overcome drug resistance and metastasis. Through lineage-tracing and lineage-ablation studies, our team has previously shown hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells marked by CD133 to represent a functional subset displaying dedifferentiated status with stemness traits, yet there are limited therapies effective for eradicating such resilient cell populations. Here, we explore the therapeutic potential of repurposing an existing drug estramustine phosphate (EMP) for targeting HCC plasticity through inhibiting MAP2, a gene uniquely enriched in CD133+ 'HCC' stemness subset but not in CD133+ 'normal' regenerative cells. MAP2 is transcriptionally activated by histone 3 lysine 27 acetylation and its upregulation correlates with aggressive clinical features. Mechanistically, MAP2 sustains tumor plasticity and transition to a mesenchymal state through inducing filamentous actin polymerization and YAP activation, which subsequently disrupts integrin expression and cell adhesions. Our research offers a promising opportunity for drug repurposing using EMP in combination with sorafenib to target HCC at its stemness roots.

articles.title: The double-edged sword of human-AI collaboration on design students' competence development: The mediating roles of challenge and hindrance appraisals and the asymmetric moderation of teacher AI leadership.
articles.authors: Xiang Wang, MingXing Li, Jia Du, Y U Yao, Jiabei Jiang
articles.abstract: The deepening integration of generative AI into design education is driving a paradigm shift in human-computer AI collaboration (HAIC) -from mere tool assistance toward intelligent synergy. However, its dual impact on the competency development of design students and the underlying mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. Grounded in the Theory of Stress Appraisal, this study constructs a research model to examine the double-edged sword effect of HAIC on Design Competence (DC), introducing teacher AI Leadership (AIL) as a moderating variable. The aim is to reveal the psychological mechanisms and boundary conditions through which HAIC influences DC. Employing a questionnaire survey, this study conducted an empirical investigation involving 483 design students in East China. Data analysis was performed using SPSS 24.0 and Amos 23.0, encompassing reliability and validity tests, regression analysis, and Bootstrap mediation analysis. The results indicate that HAIC influences DC through dual pathways: it positively enhances DC by fostering Challenge Appraisal (CA) (β = 0.283, p < 0.01), which in turn positively predicted competence development (β = 0.363, p < 0.01), yielding a significant indirect effect of 0.103 (p < 0.01). Simultaneously, HAIC triggered Hindrance Appraisal (HA) (β = 0.271, p < 0.01), which negatively predicted competence development (β = -0.229, p < 0.01), yielding a significant indirect effect of -0.062 (p < 0.01). This constitutes a partial mediating mechanism characterized by "one positive, one negative" effect. Furthermore, Teacher AIL exhibits an asymmetric moderating effect: it significantly buffers the positive impact of HAIC on HA (β = -0.112, p < 0.01), indicating that high AIL can mitigate cognitive load and anxiety arising from technological uncertainty, yet it does not significantly amplify the positive pathway via CA (β = 0.001, p > 0.05). The findings suggest that the impact of HAIC on DC is not linear but rather a dialectical process contingent upon individual cognitive appraisal. The core value of Teacher AIL lies in "risk mitigation" rather than "creativity stimulation," offering a theoretical foundation for the intelligent transformation of educational design. At the practical level, it is imperative to facilitate from knowledge deliverers to cognitive facilitators in AI-augmented design education. By systematically developing AI instructional competencies and reforming assessment systems, educators can guide students toward establishing a healthy relationship with HAIC, thereby achieving the synergistic advancement of technological empowerment and humanistic literacy.

articles.title: Interventional radiation immune-boosting (iRIB). The role of concomitant interventional radiotherapy (modern brachytherapy) in immunotherapy: A hypothesis-generating systematic review.
articles.authors: Roberta Muni, Valentina Lancellotta, Bruno Fionda, Enrico Rosa, Piotr Wojcieszek, Roberto Iacovelli, Monica Mangoni, Gabriella Macchia
articles.abstract: Synergistic activity of radiation and immunotherapy is well known to the extent that it can be referred to as radiation immuno-boosting. Interventional radiotherapy (IRT; modern brachytherapy) has a potential immunomodulatory advantage compared with external beam radiotherapy due to highly conformal dose distribution and dose heterogeneity, engaging multiple immunogenic mechanisms with distinct dose-response profiles. A hypothesis-generating systematic review was conducted in June 2026 using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science databases to identify clinical studies reporting outcomes of patients treated with IRT plus immunotherapy, including any primary tumor, assessing efficacy and toxicity. Study selection, data extraction, and risk of bias assessment were performed according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using a GRADE-based approach. Among the identified publications, 13 studies were included in qualitative synthesis. The included studies published between 2019 and 2026 were non-randomized, and comprised 98 patients with hepatocellular carcinoma, adrenocortical carcinoma, melanoma, kidney, and pancreatic or lung cancer. IRT was delivered before, concurrently, or in close temporal proximity to immunotherapy. Radiological tumor response of irradiated lesions was consistently reported, although outcome definitions were heterogeneous and often descriptive. Progression-free survival ranged from 1 to over 30 months. Severe treatment-related toxicity (grade ≥ 3) was uncommon, and no unexpected safety signals were observed. Occasional regression of non-irradiated lesions was reported; however, these observations were anecdotal and cannot be reliably attributed to radiation-induced systemic immune activation. Interventional radiotherapy has a biological rationale for potential immunomodulatory interactions with immunotherapy, but these effects have not yet been established clinically. Although current clinical evidence is limited and of very low certainty, preliminary findings support additional prospective investigation. Further prospective studies are required to better characterize the optimal integration of IRT and immunotherapy, including radiation dose, fractionation schedules, and treatment sequencing.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes after interstitial high-dose-rate brachytherapy vs. stereotactic body radiotherapy in hepatocellular carcinoma: A retrospective matched single-center analysis.
articles.authors: Sebastian Teich, Anna-Maria Bühler, Sebastian Schäfer, Philipp Geisler, Saskia Spautz, Isabell Prager, Stefan Dietzsch, Ilias Sachpazidis
articles.abstract: Interstitial high-dose-rate brachytherapy (iBT) and stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) are local treatment options for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Data comparing their efficiency and safety profile remain limited. Therefore, we aimed to compare treatment results of iBT and SBRT in HCC patients. Patients with HCC who underwent iBT or SBRT between 2014 and 2024 at our tertiary center were retrospectively analyzed. Local control (LC), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS) were evaluated. Treatment-related acute and chronic toxicities were assessed. In a cohort of 92 patients with 125 HCC lesions, 60 patients (65.2%) with 86 lesions (68.8%) were treated with iBT. The median follow-up was 21 months. There were no significant differences in LC (p = 0.73) or PFS (p = 0.27) between iBT and SBRT cohorts. To reduce confounding due to imbalances in baseline characteristics, a 1 : 1 matched sub-cohort was generated. For all patients with complete clinical data, each SBRT patient was matched to one iBT patient using a multivariable distance metric based on Charlson comorbidity index (CCI), liver cirrhosis, Child-Pugh score (CPS), albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) score, and age, resulting in two equally-sized groups with reduced baseline imbalance. After matching, the OS advantage of iBT over SBRT was no longer statistically significant. The most common acute treatment-related toxicities were grade 1 elevations of liver enzymes in the iBT group (12/60, 20%) and fatigue in the SBRT group (5/32, 15.6%). In the iBT group, two minor bleeding events and one pneumothorax occurred, but no grade > 3 late toxicity was observed. Both iBT and SBRT provide effective local treatment options for HCC, achieving comparable LC and PFS, while maintaining a manageable toxicity profile. Patient selection should be guided by institutional expertise and patient preference.

articles.title: Modern brachytherapy modalities vs. external beam radiotherapy in post-operative non-melanoma skin cancer: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Wiedya K Angeline, Hendriyo, Rudiyo, Juli Jamnasi, Sudibio, Julius Oentario, Vito Filbert Jayalie
articles.abstract: Facial non-melanoma skin cancers (NMSCs) are primarily managed surgically, but adjuvant or definitive radiotherapy is indicated for high-risk or anatomically complex lesions. While electron-based external beam radiotherapy (EBRT) remains standard, high-dose-rate (HDR) brachytherapy modalities now utilize surface moulds, 3D-printed applicators, interstitial implants, and flap techniques. This systematic review assessed the oncological efficacy, dosimetric characteristics, toxicity, and cosmetic outcomes of these brachytherapy techniques compared with EBRT. Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Semantic Scholar, Google Scholar, Springer, and Wiley Online Library for studies evaluating modern brachytherapy and EBRT in NMSC. Data on local control (LC), cosmesis, organ preservation, and toxicity were extracted and synthesized. Twenty-three studies met the inclusion criteria. Modern brachytherapy achieved local control rates of 90% to 100%, demonstrating clinical non-inferiority to EBRT. Brachytherapy exhibited a steeper dose fall-off than EBRT, facilitating target volume dose delivery while sparing adjacent organs at risk. This advantage resulted in high rates of organ preservation, notably avoiding radiation-induced cataracts in periocular applications, and favorable clinician- and patient-reported cosmetic outcomes. Utilizing 3D-printing optimized applicator conformity, and eliminated air gaps in irregular anatomical topographies. Morbidity was primarily limited to transient grade 1 or 2 acute cutaneous reactions, with severe late toxicities below 2%. Modern HDR brachytherapy provides local control equivalent to EBRT, along with superior dosimetric conformity, functional preservation, and cosmetic outcomes. Its capacity for hypofractionation also offers an operational advantage. Treatment selection requires an individualized, multidisciplinary approach based on tumor depth, anatomical complexity, and institutional capability. Future multicenter randomized controlled trials incorporating standardized patient-reported outcomes are required to validate these findings.

articles.title: Single-Session Ablative Radioembolization for Small Hepatocellular Carcinoma Is Associated with Lower Treatment-Episode Charges, Shorter Time to Treatment, and Reduced Travel Burden.
articles.authors: Shawn Thomas, Breanna Collins, Jeet Minocha, Jonas Will Redmond, Raunak Sandu, Tyler Clark Mandt, Zachary Tyler Berman
articles.journal: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
articles.abstract: To test the hypothesis that, compared with conventional two-session transarterial radioembolization (TARE), single-session TARE (ssTARE) is associated with lower hospital charges, fewer modeled interventional radiology (IR) physician work relative value units (wRVUs), shorter consultation-to-treatment intervals, and less procedure-related travel in selected patients undergoing ablative TARE for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This single-institution retrospective review included 312 treatment episodes in 255 patients between January 2022 and April 2026, comprising 96 single-session ablative TARE episodes and 216 conventional TARE episodes. Conventional TARE was defined as mapping angiography with Tc-99m MAA administration, SPECT/CT, and lung shunt fraction calculation followed by Y-90 administration during a separate encounter. Ninety-three of 96 ssTARE attempts (96.9%) had successful Y-90 delivery. All treatments used glass microspheres. Mean recorded hospital charges were $118,656 for conventional TARE (n=202) and $86,193 for ssTARE (n=51), a 27.4% reduction (p < 0.001). Lower charges persisted in sensitivity analyses. ssTARE was associated with 17.9% fewer modeled IR physician wRVUs and 42.6% fewer modeled driving miles (p < 0.01). The primary consultation-to-treatment interval was 15 days shorter (p < 0.01). In selected patients with HCC, ssTARE was associated with lower recorded institutional charges, fewer modeled procedure-related travel miles, and a shorter consultation-to-treatment interval.

articles.title: Patient selection for proton therapy in lung cancer: Updating and internal-external cross-validation of a normal tissue complication probability model for acute oesophageal toxicity.
articles.authors: R Wijsman, J G M van Loon, R Bartels, B Stam, D A X Schinagl, L Boersma, J B Reitsma, J A Langendijk
articles.journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
articles.abstract: To externally validate and update a published normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) model for the prediction of Grade ≥ 2 acute oesophageal toxicity (AOT) in lung cancer patients receiving (chemo-)radiotherapy (predictors: concurrent chemotherapy, gender, tumour stage, mean oesophagus dose (MOD)). Patient cohorts from four centres were available. Initial external validation was performed by assessing model performance. Heterogeneity of performance across cohorts was evaluated using an internal-external cross validation (IECV) method. Based on the IECV procedure, parameters were added or removed from the model to lower heterogeneity in model performance across cohorts with the aim to create a model that performed uniformly well across centres. Ridge regression was used to create the final model and bootstrapping techniques were applied to perform further internal validation. Out of 937 patients, 444 (47%) had Grade ≥ 2 AOT. External validation indicated model recalibration was necessary for 1 cohort and model revision for another. IECV showed heterogeneity of performance of the original model across cohorts. To lower heterogeneity in model performance, the predictors concurrent chemotherapy, gender, and tumour stage were removed from the model, and overall treatment time (OTT) was added. The final model containing MOD and OTT as predictors showed low levels of heterogeneity in model performance (I2 of 0% for all performance measures) with optimism-corrected AUC of 0.75, calibration intercept of -0.01 and slope of 1.26. The validation and updating of an NTCP-model for AOT resulted in a prediction model performing well in varying patient cohorts. Therefore, this updated model was added to the national indication protocol to select lung cancer patients for proton radiotherapy.

articles.title: Comprehensive clinical dosimetry in contact skin interventional radiotherapy (modern brachytherapy): Practical tips and tricks.
articles.authors: Bruno Fionda, Enrico Rosa, Elisa Placidi, Valentina Lancellotta, Pierpaolo Dragonetti, Maria Concetta La Milia, Martina De Angeli, Francesco Pastore
articles.abstract: Contact interventional radiotherapy (cIRT) is an effective option for non-melanoma skin cancers, particularly in anatomically complex sites, where organ preservation, functional results, and cosmetic outcomes are relevant. This paper summarized practical dosimetric considerations in cIRT, focusing on the therapeutic window, surface curvature, boluses and air gaps, dose calculation algorithms, and 3D-printed devices. Key physical and clinical factors affecting dose distribution were analyzed from recent literature, including prescription depth, source-to-skin distance, applicator geometry, tissue interfaces, and patient-specific device design. Therapeutic window is influenced by target thickness, source-to-skin distance, and surface curvature. Multilayer and intensity-modulated arrangements may improve target coverage while limiting superficial hotspots. Bolus and air gaps can modify local dose distribution, especially in irregular anatomical regions, while model-based algorithms better account for heterogeneities and interfaces than TG-43. 3D-printed applicators may further enhance conformity, reproducibility, and organs at risk sparing. Although clinically non-invasive, cIRT requires careful dosimetric optimization. Appropriate management of applicator geometry, dose calculation, bolus, air gaps, and patient-specific devices, may improve treatment accuracy, target coverage, and toxicity control.

articles.title: Collaborative design and additive manufacturing of a patient-specific high-dose-rate surface mold applicator for upper lip plesiotherapy.
articles.authors: Bryce Matthew Tan De Guzman, Thomas Niccolo F Reyes, Leona Marie Francesca Rebosa, Patricia Ong, Vannesza Hendricke Chua, Stellar Marie Cabrera, Maureen Bojador, Warren Bacorro
articles.abstract: To demonstrate the use of additive manufacturing in the design and fabrication of a high-dose-rate (HDR) plesiotherapy applicator for upper lip squamous cell carcinoma, with emphasis on design parameters, adequate dose coverage, and practical considerations for applicator customization. A 52-year-old male with persistent superficial upper lip squamous cell carcinoma, who previously underwent definitive chemoradiotherapy, was selected for HDR plesiotherapy boost to residual disease in an under-dosed region. Clinical measurements were performed by computer-aided design (CAD) for patient-specific surface mold incorporating pre-defined catheter geometry and mechanical features, to ensure applicator stability despite severe trismus. The applicator was fabricated using fused deposition modeling in flexible thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU). Dimensional verification, catheter patency testing, and clinical fitting were followed by conventional CT-based treatment planning. The applicator was designed and fabricated within 72 hours, and radiotherapy planning followed GEC-ESTRO recommendations. Treatment planning achieved adequate target coverage, with high-risk clinical target volume (HR-CTV) D90 > 100% of prescription and V100 > 90% while maintaining acceptable dose homogeneity (DNR: < 0.36, DHI: > 0.70). Applicator positioning was reproducible across fractions, and verified by daily clinical examination and image verification. Treatment delivery was completed without device-related complications. This report demonstrates the integration of additive manufacturing into a clinical brachytherapy workflow for a patient with upper lip squamous cell carcinoma, allowing fabrication of a patient-specific surface mold applicator with technical advantages in geometric accuracy and conformity to site-specific anatomic and functional constraints. Broader clinical implementation will require structured workflow integration, institutional planning of additive manufacturing logistics with in-house versus external production, standardization of quality assurance processes, and validation in larger clinical cohort studies.

articles.title: Frailty After Transarterial Chemoembolization for Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Cross-Sectional Study of Incidence and Associated Factors.
articles.authors: Yuying Lin, Duo Qian, Bingxin Jiang, Shanshan Zhang, Tingting Li
articles.abstract: To evaluate the incidence of and factors associated with frailty in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients after transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), with the objective to inform future personalized managements. In this cross-sectional study conducted from January to October 2025, HCC patients undergoing TACE at a tertiary hospital in Suzhou were selected by convenience sampling and completed a general information questionnaire. The Fried frailty phenotype, Nutritional Risk Screening 2002 tool, and Barthel Index for activities of daily living were comprehensively evaluated between postoperative days 1 and 4 following TACE. Factors associated with frailty after TACE were identified via univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses. Among the 312 included patients, 87 (27.9%) patients and 225 (72.1%) patients were in the frailty and non-frailty groups, respectively. Univariate analysis revealed statistically significant differences in age, sex, nutritional risk, Barthel Index, systemic immune-inflammatory index (SII), and hemoglobin level between the two groups (P<0.05). Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified that age, sex, nutritional risk, Barthel Index, SII, and hemoglobin level were associated with frailty after TACE, with odds ratios of 1.060, 4.199, 6.870, 0.954, 1.001, and 0.980, respectively (all P<0.05). A significant number of HCC patients could have frailty after TACE. Advanced age, female sex, poor nutrition, low Barthel Index, high SII, and low hemoglobin level were associated with frailty in these patients. Further prospective trials are required to identify modifiable variables and evaluate interventions to prevent or reduce frailty in HCC patients undergoing TACE.

articles.title: Recent advances in conversion therapy for hepatocellular carcinoma with portal vein tumor thrombosis.
articles.authors: Panpan Xie, Jianfang Zhu, Peng Xu, Peng Zhang, Fengguo Jian
articles.abstract: Portal vein tumor thrombosis (PVTT) is one of the most clinically consequential manifestations of advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). It reflects aggressive tumor biology, compromises portal venous inflow, and reduces the therapeutic window for locoregional intervention. Historically, macroscopic portal vein invasion generally placed patients within advanced-stage treatment pathways, in which systemic therapy constituted the standard treatment backbone and curative-intent approaches were applicable only to selected patients. This paradigm has now shifted. In recent years, the management of unresectable HCC has been reshaped by immune-based systemic therapy, more active tyrosine kinase inhibitor-based combinations, hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC), selective transarterial therapies, thrombus-directed radiotherapy, and increasingly standardized multidisciplinary conversion strategies. Consequently, a subset of patients with liver-dominant HCC and PVTT can now be downstaged to radical resection or other definitive local treatment, particularly when liver function is preserved and therapy is initiated before irreversible hepatic decompensation develops. This review summarizes recent advances in the diagnosis and classification of PVTT, the biological and technical rationale for conversion therapy, and the evolving evidence for systemic therapy, HAIC, transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), radiotherapy, triple-modality treatment, salvage surgery, and postoperative management. It also highlights key limitations, including the predominance of retrospective East Asian cohorts, heterogeneity in PVTT classification and treatment protocols, uncertainty regarding the optimal timing of surgery, and the absence of validated biomarkers for selecting patients most likely to benefit from aggressive multimodality treatment. Overall, the available evidence supports integrating response-guided multidisciplinary strategies into established evidence-based treatment frameworks for carefully selected patients. Even so, conversion therapy for HCC with PVTT remains an evidence-evolving strategy that should be applied with careful patient selection, disciplined treatment sequencing, and substantial institutional expertise rather than adopted as a universal standard of care.

articles.title: NMA plus antitumor therapy versus antitumor therapy alone in patients with BCLC stage B or C hepatocellular carcinoma and pre-cachexia or cachexia: protocol for a prospective, multicenter, randomized, open-label phase II trial.
articles.authors: Ruihong Dai, Facheng Lu, Weibing Leng, Qing He, Wenhao Guo, Tao Hai, Chang Liu
articles.abstract: Cancer anorexia-cachexia syndrome (CACS) is prevalent among patients with Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) stage B or C hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and is strongly associated with poor prognosis, reduced treatment tolerance, and impaired quality of life. Megestrol acetate (MA) has demonstrated efficacy in improving appetite and body weight; however, conventional formulations are limited by variable bioavailability. This trial will evaluate the efficacy and safety of nanocrystalline megestrol acetate (NMA) in patients with BCLC stage B or C HCC and pre-cachexia or cachexia receiving systemic therapy combined with transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) or hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC). This multicenter, randomized, open-label, parallel-group Phase II trial protocol will enroll 68 adults aged 18-75 years with BCLC stage B or C HCC and pre-cachexia or cachexia. Participants will be stratified according to BCLC stage and weight loss during the previous 6 months and then randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either NMA (625 mg/day for 12 weeks) plus antitumor therapy (systemic therapy combined with transarterial chemoembolization [TACE] or hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy [HAIC]) or antitumor therapy alone. Antitumor therapy will comprise systemic therapy combined with TACE or HAIC. The co-primary endpoints are the proportions of Anorexia/Cachexia Subscale-12 (A/CS-12) responders and body mass index (BMI) responders at Week 12. Secondary endpoints include objective response rate, progression-free survival, changes in the L3 skeletal muscle index (L3 SMI), and the incidence of adverse events. Exploratory endpoints will evaluate inflammatory and nutritional biomarkers as well as quality of life, assessed using the European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire-C30 (EORTC QLQ-C30). This trial will provide preliminary comparative data on NMA plus antitumor therapy versus antitumor therapy alone in patients with BCLC stage B or C HCC and pre-cachexia or cachexia. The study protocol was approved by the Ethics Committee of West China Hospital, Sichuan University (IRB No. 2025-2539). The trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07356037.

articles.title: Repeated metastasis-directed radiotherapy in patients with oligorecurrent prostate cancer: outcomes and risk stratification from a large multinational PSMA PET-guided cohort.
articles.authors: Ruth van der Walle, Tessa D van Bergen, Marcin Miszczyk, Max Peters, Mateusz Bilski, Giulio Francolini, Pietro Garlatti, Maris Mezeckis
articles.journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
articles.abstract: Repeated metastasis-directed radiotherapy (MDRT) is increasingly used in patients with metachronous oligometastatic prostate cancer. However, the efficacy and optimal patient selection criteria remain insufficiently defined. Within the multinational PORTAL consortium, we evaluated outcomes of repeated MDRT in patients with PSMA-PET-detected oligorecurrent hormone-sensitive prostate cancer undergoing ≥ 2 MDRT cycles. The primary endpoint was androgen deprivation therapy-free survival (ADT-FS), secondary endpoints included polymetastatic-free survival, next-line systemic therapy-free survival, and overall survival, all calculated from start of repeated MDRT. A multivariable Cox regression model was developed to predict ADT-FS, and its performance was evaluated by bootstrapped internal validation using discrimination (C-index) and calibration. A total of 177 patients were included. Median follow-up after second MDRT was 26.1 months. During follow-up, 86 patients initiated ADT, 59 developed polymetastatic disease, 38 received next-line systemic therapy, and 17 deaths occurred. Two-year ADT-FS was 50.2 % (95 % CI 41.4-58.3). Two-year polymetastatic-free, next-line systemic therapy-free, and overall survival were 64.4 % (95 % CI 55.4-72.0), 83.5 % (95 % CI 76.0-88.9), and 94.2 % (95 % CI 88.2-97.2), respectively. In the multivariable Cox regression model, a longer interval between first and second MDRT (HR 0.96 per month, 95 % CI 0.94-0.99; p = 0.003) and treatment of a single versus ≥ 2 new lesions (HR for ≥ 2 lesions 1.88, 95 % CI 1.22-2.90; p = 0.006) were independently associated with ADT-FS. Model discrimination was moderate (optimism-corrected C-index 0.68) with good calibration. In this multicentre cohort of patients with PSMA PET-detected metachronous oligorecurrent prostate cancer undergoing repeated MDRT, favourable ADT-FS outcomes were observed, with approximately half of patients remaining ADT-free two years after second MDRT. Given the absence of a comparator group, these outcomes may reflect both the effects of treatment and favourable disease biology of patients who remained eligible for repeated MDRT. The interval between MDRT cycles, and the number of metastases, independently predicted ADT-FS and may support patient selection.

articles.title: Transarterial chemoembolization combined with sorafenib versus monotherapy for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma: An umbrella review of meta-analyses.
articles.authors: Vikash Kumar Karmani, Syeda Fatima Murtaza, Mariana Paz Aviles, Divyashish Bhardwaj, Aleena Majeed, Araj Naveed Siddiqui, Areej Dar, Aalam Sohal
articles.abstract: This umbrella review synthesizes evidence from meta-analyses and reviews comparing transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) combined with sorafenib versus monotherapy for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma. Following PRIOR guidelines, PubMed, Google Scholar, Web of Science, and Embase were searched from inception to December 2024. Outcomes included overall survival (OS), time to progression (TTP), disease control rate (DCR), and objective response rate (ORR). Corrected covered area (CCA) assessed overlap, and methodological quality was evaluated using AMSTAR-2. Of 13,821 records, 9 meta-analyses were included, with substantial overlap (CCA: 49%). Eight reviews assessed OS; five reported a significant survival benefit (hazard ratio [HR] 0.62-0.74, p < 0.001), while two found no significant effect (HR 0.75-0.97, p > 0.05). Eight evaluated TTP; six showed a significant reduction in risk (HR 0.61-0.75, p < 0.05), while two reported non-significant findings (HR 0.74-0.77, p > 0.05). Four assessed DCR; two reported a significant benefit (odds ratio [OR] 0.52-4.72, p < 0.01), one showed a non-significant trend (OR: 1.57, p = 0.06), and one found no significant effect (relative risk [RR] 1.04, p = 0.57). Six assessed ORR; three reported a significant increase in response (OR 2.19-3.59, p < 0.01), one showed a significant reduction (OR 0.85, p < 0.001), one found no significant effect (RR 1.20, p = 0.26), and one reported a significant protective effect (OR 0.39, p = 0.008). TACE plus sorafenib improves TTP, ORR, and OS in unresectable HCC and highlights the need for personalized treatment and further research.

articles.title: The neogenin-hemojuvelin axis in murine liver is crucial for hepcidin expression.
articles.authors: Caroline A Enns, Shall Jue, Bethel Demissu, An-Sheng Zhang
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Gastrointestinal and liver physiology
articles.abstract: Neogenin (NEO1) is a ubiquitously expressed, multifunctional receptor that binds hemojuvelin (HJV); both proteins are essential components within hepatocytes for maintaining systemic iron homeostasis. Previous research established that the targeted ablation of hepatic Neo1 or Hjv in mice markedly reduces expression of the central iron-regulatory hormone, hepcidin. Reduction in hepcidin results in unrestricted iron absorption that leads to severe systemic iron overload. Hepatic hepcidin expression is primarily induced via the bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) signaling pathway, which requires a complex of plasma membrane proteins, including HJV acting as a BMP coreceptor. However, the precise mechanism by which NEO1 and HJV are orchestrated to robustly activate this pathway remains poorly understood. In this study, we systemically investigated the mechanisms by which hepatic Neo1 coordinates with Hjv to facilitate hepcidin induction using various knockout mouse models. Our data indicate that although Hjv is a more potent inducer of hepcidin than hepatic Neo1, the simultaneous ablation of both Neo1 and Hjv greatly reduces hepcidin expression. These results suggest that these two proteins form a crucial functional axis for controlling hepcidin levels. Further analysis revealed that ∼84% of hepcidin expression relies on the synergistic association of Neo1 with Hjv. In comparison, Hjv retains a significantly compromised (∼12%) ability to induce hepcidin independently of Neo1, whereas Neo1 possesses only a residual (∼3%) independent induction capacity. Collectively, these data support a model in which hepatic Neo1 acts primarily as a molecular scaffold to facilitate assembly of the hepcidin-inducing signaling complex through Hjv.NEW & NOTEWORTHY Hepcidin expression in hepatocytes relies on a multiprotein plasma membrane complex. This study establishes a critical functional axis between neogenin and hemojuvelin within this complex, revealing how their coordination is essential for systemic iron homeostasis. Our findings provide a new mechanistic framework for understanding the assembly of the hepcidin-signaling complex.

articles.title: Selective lipid Metabolic remodelling in radiosensitive normal tissues after FLASH radiotherapy.
articles.authors: Shuhei Aramaki, Maxime Dubail, Mathieu Sertorio, Md Muedur Rahman, Mst Sayela Afroz, Chi Zhang, Liang Tang, Kohei Wakabayashi
articles.journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
articles.abstract: FLASH radiotherapy, delivered at ultra-high dose rates, spares normal tissues while maintaining tumor control, but the molecular basis of this differential response remains poorly defined, particularly at timepoints relevant to tissue repair. We investigated whether lipid metabolism contributes to the FLASH effect in head and neck cancer. MOC2 tumor-bearing mice received a single 10 Gy fraction of conventional (CONV) or ultra-high dose-rate FLASH protons, with non-irradiated controls (CTRL). Tongue and contralateral tumors were collected two weeks later and analyzed by bulk lipidomics, spatial lipidomics and proteomics. After biochemical filtering, 1,547 lipid species across 37 classes were quantified. At two weeks, CONV irradiation was associated with a triglyceride-catabolic, oxidative-stress signature in tongue tissue, marked by loss of the lipid-droplet hydrolase Ces1d alongside induction of the peroxisomal β-oxidation enzyme Acox1. FLASH irradiation was instead associated with a distinct lipid-remodelling signature: suppression of Mgll, induction of Apoe, membrane phospholipid remodelling (increased phosphatidylcholine and phosphatidylethanolamine), and Lypla2 upregulation. Spatial lipidomics provided illustrative spatial context consistent with concentration of these changes in minor salivary gland acini. Tumor tissue showed no comparable modality-specific divergence. These correlative multi-omics data indicate that FLASH is associated with remodelling of lipid metabolism in radiosensitive normal tissue, beyond a simple reduction of acute oxidative damage. We propose a Lipid Metabolic Remodelling Hypothesis for testing: the remodelling of lipid metabolism observed after FLASH may contribute to normal-tissue sparing rather than representing solely a downstream consequence of reduced acute oxidative damage. This model complements existing physicochemical models and offers a basis for radioprotection strategies in head and neck radiotherapy.

articles.title: Socioeconomic inequalities in treatment for colorectal liver metastases in England: A competing risk analysis using National Cancer Registration Dataset.
articles.authors: Mari Kajiwara Saito, Manuela Quaresma, Hadrien Charvat, Aurélien Belot, Eyad Issa, Bernard Rachet
articles.abstract: There has been a wide variation, as well as socioeconomic inequalities, in liver resection rate for people diagnosed with colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) in England. Currently, service specification in England requires providers to follow locally agreed referral pathways. However, decisions about patient referral to specialist multi-disciplinary teams (MDTs) may depend on local primary site-specific MDTs. We aimed to assess socioeconomic inequalities in the probability of undergoing liver resection/ablation (liver treatment), among patients diagnosed with synchronous/metachronous liver metastases (sLM/mLM). We identified patients diagnosed with colorectal cancer from 2015 to 2022 using the National Cancer Registration Dataset, and those with CRLM using the administrative dataset. We conducted a competing-risk analysis using flexible parametric regression models to estimate liver treatment-specific hazard up to one year after CRLM diagnosis by SES. We also derived cumulative probabilities of receiving treatment (CPrLtx), handling death as the competing event. The population-level CPrLtx was 8.7% (95% confidence interval [CI] 8.5 to 9.0%) for sLM (36 660 patients) and 23.5% (95% CI 23.1 to 24.0%) for mLM (25 159 patients). The adjusted CPrLtx gap between the least and most deprived groups reached 2.6% (1.8 to 3.5%) for sLM and 1.0% (95% CI -0.2 to 2.3%) for mLM. Socioeconomic inequalities in liver treatment receipt persisted for sLM. Referral of all patients with CRLM to hepato-pancreato-biliary (HPB) specialists is recommended, irrespective of SES of patients. Potential policy lever could be promoting proactive HPB specialist involvement in local colorectal multi-disciplinary meetings to reduce variation in referral. (250 words).

articles.title: Low-duty-cycle pulsed ultrasound for ex vivo liver tissue ablation: thermal safety, lesion conformity, and vascular structure preservation.
articles.authors: Xiao Li, Ke Wu, Zhenxin Shen, Yankun Yan, Weihong Meng, Dongya Yang, Hongyan Duan
articles.abstract: To investigate the physical mechanisms and engineering efficacy of low-duty-cycle pulsed ultrasound (histotripsy) in overcoming the heat sink effect and preserving major hepatic vessels.Impact Statement: This study provides a highly conformal, non-thermal ablation strategy that eliminates blood flow cooling effects while maintaining vascular integrity, offering superior precision over traditional methods. Conventional thermal ablation for hepatocellular carcinoma is limited by the "heat sink effect," causing marginal residual tumors and risking irreversible damage to major blood vessels. Quantitative investigations defining the thermal safety boundaries of histotripsy to overcome these limitations are currently lacking. Combining simulation optimization and ex-vivo validation, an acoustic-thermal coupled model identified an optimal protocol (2.0 MHz, 37 MPa, 0.5% duty cycle). Ex-vivo porcine liver experiments compared this cavitation ablation head-to-head with continuous-wave thermal ablation near major vessels, assessing morphology, Conformity Index (CI), and vascular integrity. Simulations showed a 0.5% duty cycle kept peak temperatures below the 60°C denaturation threshold. Ex-vivo, the cavitation group achieved homogeneous liquefaction, sharp boundaries, and preserved adjacent vessels, yielding a 96.8 ± 2.1% CI. The thermal group suffered from the cooling effect, showing irregular defects and a lower CI of 71.2 ± 15.6% (P < 0.01). Low-duty-cycle pulsed ultrasound provides a safe, highly conformal non-thermal ablation solution that successfully overcomes the heat sink effect and preserves critical vascular architecture.

articles.title: Epigenetically silencing gluconeogenic enzyme PCK1 by EZH2 promotes renal tubulointerstitial fibrosis.
articles.authors: Ming Wu, Pinglan Lin, Zhiqiang Yan, Yanzhe Wang, Anna Rinaldi, Pietro E Cippà, Di Huang, Jiayi Qiao
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a leading cause of global morbidity. The kidney is a major gluconeogenic organ, and impaired renal gluconeogenesis contributes to CKD, yet the regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here we show that enhancer of zeste homolog 2 (EZH2), a histone H3K27 trimethyltransferase, epigenetically suppresses renal gluconeogenesis and drives tubulointerstitial fibrosis. Through integrative multi-omics profiling (RNA-seq, CUT&Tag, and single-nucleus RNA-seq), we show that EZH2 directly binds to and deposits H3K27 trimethylation at promoters of gluconeogenic genes in proximal tubular cells, with the most prominent repression observed at phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase (Pck1) gene. In fibrotic kidneys, Ezh2 is markedly upregulated in proximal tubules and inversely correlates with Pck1 expression across injury and maladaptive repair states. Genetic ablation or pharmacological inhibition of EZH2 restores PCK1 expression, enhances lactate-to-glucose conversion, and attenuates extracellular matrix deposition and fibrotic marker expression in both cultured tubular cells and mouse models of kidney fibrosis. Stable isotope 13C-lactate tracing shows that tubular Ezh2 deletion increases the labelling fractions of gluconeogenic intermediates while reducing the labelling fraction of acetyl-CoA, indicating preferential partitioning of lactate-derived carbon towards gluconeogenesis rather than oxidative entry into the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle in vivo. Mechanistically, Pck1 gain- and loss-of-function experiments establish PCK1 as a non-redundant downstream effector of EZH2's pro-fibrotic action. Collectively, our findings uncover an EZH2-PCK1 epigenetic-metabolic axis that couples histone methylation to gluconeogenic reprogramming and fibrogenesis. This axis may offer a dual therapeutic opportunity for CKD by concurrently restoring metabolic homeostasis and limiting fibrotic progression.

articles.title: ARID2 Loss Reprograms the Kynurenine-AhR Pathway to Restore Antitumor Immunity in CTNNB1-Mutant Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
articles.authors: Qianyu Li, Yunfeng Yuan, Ning Liu, Linfeng Li, Yifei Qian, Fan Wang, Songling Li, Wenli Qin
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) driven by gain-of-function mutations in CTNNB1 (CTNNB1GOF) that stabilize β-catenin exhibits a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), rendering it resistant to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). Metabolic reprogramming is increasingly recognized as a crucial mediator of immune activity, highlighting the need to elucidate the specific metabolic mechanisms underlying immune exclusion in CTNNB1GOF HCC. Here, we identified a critical metabolic-immune network orchestrated by co-mutations of CTNNB1 and ARID2. Integrative analysis of HCC patient cohorts and a de novo MYC/CTNNB1GOF HCC mouse model revealed that tumors harboring concurrent CTNNB1 and ARID2 mutations exhibited a more immune-active TME and improved survival compared to tumors with CTNNB1 mutations alone. Mechanistically, β-catenin and ARID2 cooperatively enhanced the transcription of tryptophan 2,3-dioxygenase (TDO2), leading to accelerated kynurenine production and activation of the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) in myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs). This metabolic axis established an immunosuppressive milieu characterized by MDSC accumulation and impaired T cell function. Genetic ablation of Arid2 in CTNNB1GOF HCC attenuated TDO2-dependent kynurenine synthesis, reduced MDSC infiltration, and enhanced CD8⁺ T cell cytotoxicity, thereby sensitizing tumors to anti-PD-1 therapy. Clinically, co-mutations of CTNNB1 and ARID2 correlated with elevated immune infiltration and favorable ICB responses across multiple human cancers, including HCC. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of AhR phenocopied the immunomodulatory effect of ARID2 loss and, when combined with anti-PD-1, robustly reversed the immune-cold phenotype of CTNNB1GOF HCC. These findings reveal TDO2-kynurenine-AhR signaling as a pivotal metabolic pathway enforcing immune evasion in CTNNB1-mutant HCC.

articles.title: Durable Response to Vebreltinib in Heavily Pretreated MET-Amplified Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma: A Case Report.
articles.authors: Yingying Hang, Lu Bai, Hsiquan Hsu, Ying Chen, Fufeng Wang, Wuyan Xu, Xia Zhen, Zihao Wang
articles.abstract: MET amplification, although detected in only 2% to 5% of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinomas (ICC), represents an actionable oncogenic driver. Treatment options after failure of first-line immunochemotherapy remain limited, and clinical data on vebreltinib, a novel highly selective MET inhibitor, in this molecular subset are scarce. A 61-year-old woman with metastatic ICC harboring high-level MET amplification (tissue gene copy number, 26.79) experienced disease progression on first-line durvalumab plus gemcitabine/cisplatin, second-line liposomal irinotecan/fluorouracil plus lenvatinib and durvalumab, radiotherapy, and transarterial chemoembolization. Following a brief period of vebreltinib (200 mg twice daily) plus durvalumab that was interrupted by grade 4 myelosuppression, the patient continued on vebreltinib monotherapy after hematologic recovery. Restaging computed tomography demonstrated a partial response (PR), with carbohydrate antigen 19-9 normalizing (a 99.2% reduction). This response lasted over six months until eventual disease progression. To our knowledge, this is the first report of vebreltinib monotherapy inducing a deep and durable partial response in heavily pretreated, MET-amplified ICC, with the response lasting over six months despite eventual disease progression. This case underscores the critical value of comprehensive molecular profiling after first-line treatment failure to identify actionable drivers such as MET amplification.

articles.title: Sequential Multimodal Therapy for Conversion Resection of Stage IIIa Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Case Report.
articles.authors: Yanxin Li, Ji Luo, Jinping Yang, Jianyong Zhang, Minqiang Sun, Shimin Zhang
articles.abstract: To explore the feasibility and clinical value of conversion resection after sequential comprehensive therapy consisting of transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), targeted therapy, immunotherapy and radiotherapy in patients with initially advanced stage IIIa hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The clinical data of a 61-year-old male patient with massive stage IIIa HCC accompanied by right portal vein tumor thrombus were retrospectively analyzed. The maximum diameter of the primary tumor was approximately 10.0 cm at initial diagnosis. The patient received sequential combination therapy of TACE plus targeted-immunotherapy for 8 months, followed by liver tumor radiotherapy about 1 month and maintenance targeted-immunotherapy for 12 months. After sustained tumor shrinkage, radical resection was performed on March 13, 2026. Following sequential multimodal treatment, the maximum tumor diameter decreased from 10.0 cm to 4.0 cm × 3.6 cm, achieving partial response (PR). The tumor was successfully downstaged to resectable status, and the patient recovered smoothly postoperatively without severe complications. Sequential comprehensive therapy combining TACE, targeted-immunotherapy and radiotherapy can significantly downstage initially advanced stage IIIa HCC, create opportunities for curative resection, and potentially improve long-term prognosis of patients.

articles.title: Tonsillar metastasis from hepatocellular carcinoma: a case report and literature review.
articles.authors: Jianhao Yang, Yujuan Dai, Lusheng Wen, Cuiyu Hu, Guomin Zhang
articles.abstract: Tonsillar metastasis from hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is extremely rare. We report an 84-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B who presented with a right-lobe HCC and portal vein tumor thrombosis. Three months after diagnosis, intrahepatic metastases were treated with transarterial chemoembolization and lenvatinib. Twenty-three months later, he developed blood-tinged sputum; imaging and laryngoscopy revealed a left tonsillar mass with concurrent pulmonary and hepatic progression. Tonsillectomy yielded an undifferentiated carcinoma lesion. Compared with the primary tumor, the tonsillar metastasis lost hepatocyte specific antigen (Hep Par-1) and Arginase-1 expression, showed a markedly elevated Ki-67 index (80%), but retained Glypican-3 and heat shock protein 70 (HSP70). A diagnosis of metastatic HCC was favored based on integration of clinical history, laboratory findings, and pathological immunohistochemistry. In HCC patients, any unusual head and neck lesion warrants suspicion of metastasis; a multi-marker panel is critical for diagnosis, as loss of Arginase-1 does not rule out HCC.

articles.title: A hepatic malignant spindle-cell neoplasm of uncertain lineage clinically favoring sarcomatoid hepatocellular carcinoma: a case report.
articles.authors: Haowen Li, Shengwei Li, Maohe Yu, Xin Wei, Hao Wang, Yuting Wang, Bo Liu, Lve Cheng
articles.abstract: Sarcomatoid hepatocellular carcinoma (SHC) is an uncommon and aggressive variant of primary liver cancer. Its clinical and radiological features are often nonspecific, and it may mimic inflammatory liver lesions. Evidence for unresectable SHC is limited, so management is frequently individualized. A 43-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B presented with recurrent right upper abdominal discomfort and 3 kg weight loss over 1 month. He was provisionally diagnosed with a hepatic abscess at an outside hospital, and percutaneous aspiration and drainage were performed; however, microbiological confirmation and detailed treatment records were unavailable. On admission, he had no fever or jaundice. C-reactive protein (CRP) was elevated, procalcitonin (PCT) was low, serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) remained below 12 ng/mL, and liver function was child-pugh class A. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) showed multiple right hepatic lesions with suspected invasion of adjacent portal vein branches. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated an irregular heterogeneous mass measuring approximately 88×85 mm. Because the clinicoradiological pattern was not fully consistent with simple infection, ultrasound-guided biopsy was performed. Biopsy revealed a hepatic malignant spindle-cell tumor. The initial pathological report noted limited tissue volume and atypical immunohistochemical expression, making definitive subclassification difficult. After integrated clinicopathological review, the lesion was interpreted as a malignant spindle-cell tumor clinically favoring SHC. The unresectable tumor was treated with transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC) with fluorouracil, leucovorin, and oxaliplatin (FOLFOX), lenvatinib 8 mg orally once daily, and tislelizumab 200 mg every 2 weeks. Adverse events were mainly nausea, vomiting, and right upper quadrant (RUQ) pain. Follow-up imaging showed reduction to approximately 70×58 mm and stable disease by response evaluation criteria in solid tumors (RECIST) 1.1. A hepatic malignant spindle-cell tumor clinically favoring SHC should be considered when a presumed liver abscess has atypical imaging findings, low infectious concordance, suspected vascular involvement, or poor diagnostic coherence. Early biopsy is critical. Multimodal therapy may be feasible in selected unresectable cases, but a single case cannot establish efficacy or define the contribution of each treatment component.

articles.authors: Yang Gao, Yao Wei, Hengxiao Lu, Linlin Ji
articles.abstract: Yttrium-90 microsphere selective internal radiation therapy (Y90-SIRT) is a common local interventional treatment for hepatocellular Carcinoma and liver metastases. This rare sequela emphasizes rigorous preoperative vascular evaluation, long-term monitoring and timely intervention, particularly for patients undergoing combined targeted treatment.

articles.title: The ablation margin as a regenerative and immunosuppressive niche in hepatocellular carcinoma: multicellular remodeling and organoid-on-a-chip modeling.
articles.authors: Tingyue Qiao, Yang Zha, Honghua Dai, Yue Chai, Li Weng
articles.abstract: Thermal ablation is an important local treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet post-ablation local tumor progression remains a major obstacle to durable disease control. Traditionally, recurrence has been attributed mainly to incomplete thermal coverage, inadequate ablative margins, or heat-sink effects. However, increasing evidence suggests that the sublethal thermal injury (STI) zone at the ablation margin is not merely a passive physical boundary, but a biologically active injury-repair microenvironment. Within this region, gradients of thermal dose, hypoxia, damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs), extracellular matrix mechanics, and immune infiltration may interact to shape residual tumor cell behavior. Post-ablation remodeling is likely driven by coordinated crosstalk among myeloid cells, hepatic stellate cells/cancer-associated fibroblast-like stromal cells (HSCs/CAFs), endothelial cells, neutrophils, adaptive immune cells, and residual tumor cells. These interactions may promote epithelial-mesenchymal transition, stem-like plasticity, immune evasion, angiogenic repair, and local tumor progression. Current two-dimensional (2D) cultures lack three-dimensional architecture and multicellular spatial interactions, whereas animal models are limited by variable thermal dose control, restricted real-time imaging, and interspecies differences. Emerging HCC organoid-on-a-chip platforms may help address these gaps by integrating patient-derived organoids (PDOs), tunable extracellular matrix hydrogels, microfluidic thermal and hypoxic gradients, and defined multicellular co-culture modules. Importantly, immune checkpoint testing requires immune-competent extensions incorporating autologous T cells, and antigen-presentation studies require dendritic cells. This review discusses the ablation margin as a multicellular recurrence niche and evaluates organoid-on-a-chip systems as hypothesis-generating tools for mechanism-guided and safety-conscious adjuvant strategy development.

articles.title: Value of tumor burden score combined with alpha-fetoprotein stratification in transarterial chemoembolization plus tyrosine kinase inhibitors and immune checkpoint inhibitors as triple conversion therapy for patients with initially unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma: a multicenter retrospective study (GUIDANCE010).
articles.authors: Zhi-Cheng Li, Cai-Hua Li, Da-Long Yang, Jia-Yong Su, Shao-Ping Liu, Lin Ye, Ning Peng, Fan-Jian Zeng
articles.journal: European journal of surgical oncology : the journal of the European Society of Surgical Oncology and the British Association of Surgical Oncology
articles.abstract: Currently, transarterial chemoembolization plus tyrosine kinase inhibitors and immune checkpoint inhibitors (triple conversion therapy) has demonstrated remarkable efficacy in patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC). However, the optimal beneficiary population remains unclear. This study aims to combine the tumor burden score with alpha-fetoprotein to establish a novel scoring system (tumor burden-alpha-fetoprotein, TBA) and identify the optimal beneficiaries of this therapy. Data were collected from 359 patients with uHCC who received triple conversion therapy across 17 medical centers in China. Patients were stratified into low (n = 124), medium (n = 140), and high (n = 95) TBA groups, with subsequent prognostic comparisons performed among the three groups. The higher TBA was associated with lower overall survival (OS) (medium vs. low: hazard ratio (HR) = 2.31, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.30-4.12; high vs. medium: HR = 3.92, 95% CI: 2.17-7.09); the higher TBA was associated with lower progression-free survival (PFS) (medium vs. low: HR = 1.77, 95% CI: 1.23-2.56; high vs. medium: HR = 2.35, 95% CI: 1.59-3.49). In the subgroup analysis of patients who didn't undergo hepatectomy, there were significant differences in OS and PFS among the different TBA groups, but not among those who underwent hepatectomy. articles.title: Comparative outcomes of radical prostatectomy, radiotherapy, and radiotherapy plus androgen deprivation therapy for high-risk and very high-risk prostate cancer: a narrative review.
articles.authors: Kaung Hset Tun, Xingyu Xiong, Hang Xu, Lu Yang
articles.abstract: High-risk and very high-risk prostate cancer (PCa) accounts for approximately 15-20% of newly diagnosed cases and are associated with substantial risk of disease progression, metastasis, and cancerspecific mortality. The comparative effectiveness of radical prostatectomy (RP), external beam radiotherapy (EBRT), and radiotherapy combined with androgen deprivation therapy (RT + ADT) remains uncertain because randomized head-to-head trials are lacking. This narrative review aims to synthesize the comparative effectiveness of RP, EBRT, and RT + ADT in patients with high-risk and very high-risk PCa, with respect to survival outcomes, optimal ADT duration, and toxicity/quality-of-life profiles. Literature searches were conducted across PubMed, Cochrane Library (CENTRAL), and ClinicalTrials.gov through May 2026. Studies comparing RP, EBRT, and/or RT + ADT in patients with high-risk PCa [prostate-specific antigen (PSA) ≥20 ng/mL, Gleason score 8-10/International Society of Urological Pathology (ISUP) grade ≥4, or clinical stage ≥T3a] were included. Primary outcomes were overall survival (OS), prostate cancer-specific survival (PCSS), and biochemical recurrence-free survival (bRFS). Observational studies comparing RP and RT-based strategies have reported conflicting results for OS: some studies reported more favorable outcomes with RP [hazard ratio (HR) 1.60, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.25-2.05 for EBRT + ADT vs. RP], whereas others reported more favorable outcomes with RT-based strategies (HR 1.22, 95% CI: 1.05-1.43 for RP vs. EBRT plus brachytherapy). For patients with Gleason score 9-10 disease, observational analyses suggested that EBRT with brachytherapy boost was associated with lower prostate cancer-specific mortality compared with RP (HR 0.38, 95% CI: 0.21-0.68). For RT-treated patients, randomized controlled trials (RCTs) support the use of 18-24 months of ADT. Quality-of-life analyses consistently showed worse urinary incontinence and sexual dysfunction after RP, worse bowel symptoms after RT, and compounded toxicity with multimodal therapy. For patients with high-risk and very high-risk PCa, radiotherapy combined with 18-24 months of ADT is supported by evidence from randomized trials compared with radiotherapy alone. Comparative survival evidence between RP and RT-based strategies remains conflicting and is limited by observational designs and selection bias. Treatment selection should be individualized according to patient age, comorbidity burden, tumor characteristics, and quality-of-life preferences. Randomized trials directly comparing contemporary RP with modern RT + ADT are urgently needed.

articles.title: Limited incremental value and cross-cohort transferability of CT radiomics for survival prediction after TACE in hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.authors: Krzysztof Bartnik, Belgutei Tsevegmed
articles.abstract: To evaluate whether pretreatment CT radiomics adds information for overall survival (OS) prediction among patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) treated with transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), and assess frozen imaging-model performance in an independent cohort. This retrospective study included 221 WAW-TACE and 98 HCC-TACE-SEG patients with pretreatment arterial and portal venous CT. Incremental value of a tumor-radiomics Random Survival Forest score (R1) beyond cohort-specific clinical Cox models (C0) was evaluated within each cohort using 5-fold cross-validation repeated 10 times. External validation was restricted to frozen WAW-trained R1 models (Top-K = 5, 10, 15) applied to HCC-TACE-SEG without refitting; the combined C0 + R1 model was not externally validated. WAW-TACE included 162 deaths and HCC-TACE-SEG 86 deaths. In WAW-TACE, C0, R1 Top-K = 15, and C0 + R1 achieved C-indices of 0.646 ± 0.043, 0.593 ± 0.049, and 0.639 ± 0.045, respectively. Corresponding HCC-TACE-SEG estimates were 0.496 ± 0.087, 0.530 ± 0.072, and 0.495 ± 0.094. Thus, R1 did not consistently improve cohort-specific clinical reference models. In frozen external application, Top-K = 5, 10, and 15 achieved C-indices of 0.463 (95% CI 0.397-0.532), 0.535 (0.468-0.608), and 0.528 (0.460-0.598), respectively. The evaluated models showed no consistent incremental value for OS prediction within these TACE cohorts and limited frozen-model discrimination in the clinically distinct HCC-TACE-SEG cohort. These findings do not support clinical use of these models or establish a general limitation of CT radiomics.

articles.title: Machine learning-assisted monitoring of radiofrequency ablation in hepatic tumors using spectral traces.
articles.authors: Ramy Abdlaty, Mohamed Basyouny, Mohamed Abbass
articles.abstract: Accurate intraoperative assessment of radiofrequency ablation (RFA) margins in hepatic malignancies remains a significant clinical challenge. This study investigates the efficacy of hyperspectral imaging (HSI) for objective, spatially resolved discrimination of ablated tissue, viable tumor, and normal parenchyma in 10 ex vivo liver specimens. Analysis of visible-near-infrared (VNIR) reflectance revealed distinct spectral signatures, characterized by a consistent monotonic hierarchy (ablated < normal < tumor), enabling reliable tissue differentiation. Segmentation performance was systematically evaluated using four supervised classifiers: Spectral Angle Mapper (SAM), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA). The total delineated tissue area exhibited notable inter-method variability, ranging from 137,283 to 189,289 pixels (+ 37.9%), underscoring sensitivity to classifier architecture. Nevertheless, all approaches maintained biologically coherent tissue distributions, with normal parenchyma predominating (44-56%), followed by tumor (25-39%) and ablated regions (17-20%). That is consistently indicating the necessity for monitoring ablative margins. SAM, SVM, and LDA classifiers achieved class-specific detection errors around 3.5% and 18%. LDA attained the highest overall accuracy (94.5%), demonstrating the potential of HSI for reliable, intraoperative image-guided tissue characterization. Dimensionality reduction across 462 spectral bands identified an optimal discriminative window within 643-698 nm, supporting the development of streamlined multispectral systems. Overall, HSI is neither a contact nor destructive modality for quantitative RFA assessment. Despite classifier-dependent variability necessitating standardized or ensemble strategies, these findings support its prospective integration into real-time surgical guidance, pending in vivo validation.

articles.title: IHPBA 2026 global guideline for the management of hepatocellular carcinoma in resource-constrained healthcare settings.
articles.authors: Ajith K Siriwardena, Eduard Jonas, Glenn Bonney, Shridhar Iyer, John Primrose, Rafik Filobbos, Paleswan Lakhey, T P Kingham
articles.journal: HPB : the official journal of the International Hepato Pancreato Biliary Association
articles.abstract: Current guidelines for the management of patients with HCC are predominantly focused on well-resourced healthcare systems. In 2024, the IHPBA Legacy committee initiated a process to develop global resource-sensitive guidelines for the management of HCC. An IHPBA global guideline group produced and circulated statements on the management of HCC from diagnosis to treatment, discussed these in online webinars and generated guidelines. This document focuses on the diagnosis and management of patients with HCC in resource-constrained healthcare settings. Initial diagnosis by ultrasound is supported by cross-sectional imaging. Alfa-feto protein and assessment of liver synthetic function are recommended at diagnosis. Lesion biopsy is not mandated. Liver resection is the recommended treatment of choice for single HCC in patients with preserved liver function and up to 3 lesions ≤3 cm. Radiofrequency and microwave are regarded as equivalent and can be used if resection is not available. Ethanol injection can be used if thermal ablation is not available but should be restricted to small lesions. TACE and TAE can be used for intermediate stage disease. Atezolizumab/bevacizumab combination is recommended as first line systemic therapy with sorafenib and Lenvatinib being recommended if first line is not an option. Advice for the care of the patient with advanced or terminal disease is provided. This document provides resource-sensitive HCC guidelines that prioritise feasibility, maximise benefit, and reduce default reliance on best supportive care alone and are produced for the IHPBA by discussion with the global community of IHPBA.

articles.title: Predictive target of portal pressure reduction and clinical significance of the portal vein thrombosis subgroup for hepatic encephalopathy after TIPS in decompensated cirrhosis.
articles.authors: Di Ran, Yuxia Feng, Ya Chen, Jie Yang
articles.abstract: Portal pressure reduction magnitude (ΔPVP) is a key hemodynamic indicator during transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) procedures, but its relationship with post-TIPS hepatic encephalopathy remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to determine the optimal intraoperative ΔPVP threshold for predicting post-TIPS hepatic encephalopathy. A total of patients who underwent TIPS were retrospectively analyzed. The optimal ΔPVP threshold was identified using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. ΔPVP showed a reverse L-shaped association with post-TIPS hepatic encephalopathy, and a ΔPVP threshold of 20 cmH₂O was identified. Patients achieving ΔPVP ≥ 20 cmH₂O had a lower risk of post-TIPS hepatic encephalopathy, particularly in the absence of portal vein thrombosis (PVT). Intraoperative ΔPVP ≥ 20 cmH₂O may serve as a clinically useful target for patients without PVT. External multicenter validation is required to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Peri-interventional neutrophil extracellular traps and immune surveillance in hepatocellular carcinoma: mechanisms, biomarkers, and recurrence after liver resection or thermal ablation.
articles.authors: Hang Xu, Jiayang Yi, Wanwan Zhang, Shaojie Zhu, Zhigang Liu
articles.abstract: Recurrence remains common after curative-intent liver resection or thermal ablation for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). These interventions transiently remodel the hepatic and treatment-bed immune microenvironment through overlapping but distinct processes, including tissue injury, vascular and coagulation activation, neutrophil recruitment, and, particularly during resection, hepatic ischemia-reperfusion. We organize the evidence using a peri-interventional two-component heuristic: chronic liver disease and tumor-associated inflammation may shape baseline susceptibility, whereas acute treatment injury may trigger intervention-specific neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) accumulation. Experimental studies across liver-intervention and cross-cancer models link NETs to impaired CD8+ T-cell immunity, tumor-cell retention, extracellular-matrix remodeling, and metabolic adaptation. Patient-linked evidence remains limited and largely associative; much of the mechanistic framework therefore relies on colorectal liver metastasis and cross-cancer models. Translational studies should distinguish monitoring, pharmacodynamic, prognostic, and predictive applications and prioritize serial MPO-DNA as the best-supported circulating peri-interventional candidate, with NE-DNA or H3Cit-based measures as supportive assays and spatial validation where feasible. Candidate preclinical approaches include limiting NET formation, degrading established NET structures, and disrupting NET-target-cell signaling. NET-checkpoint combinations remain preclinical hypotheses, particularly because current phase III adjuvant ICI studies have not established postoperative HCC benefit. Because NET and neutrophil functions are context dependent, prospective studies should define intervention-specific NET kinetics, immune correlates, target engagement, recurrence phenotype, and safety.

articles.title: Gefitinib-based therapy in refractory hepatocellular carcinoma with EGFR overexpression: a spatial profiling-guided case report.
articles.authors: Qin Xu, Xiaofen Li, Rui Zhu, Zirui Wang, Nuerye Tuerhonga, Chengjian Zhao, Yu Yang
articles.abstract: Current systemic treatments for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) such as antiangiogenic targeted therapies, immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), and their combinations have shown benefit, but widespread drug resistance severely limits patient outcomes and underscores an urgent need for effective post-progression strategies. We herein present a case of a patient with advanced HCC who developed cutaneous, pulmonary, and lymphatic metastases following failure of multiple lines of tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) including donafenib and regorafenib, and lenvatinib plus anti-programmed death-1 (PD-1) monoclonal antibody (tislelizumab) alongside radiotherapy. Next-generation sequencing (NGS) of the primary liver surgical sample confirmed wild-type EGFR status without canonical driver mutations, whereas retrospective immunohistochemistry (IHC) and cyclic multiplexed tyramide signal amplification (CmTSA) of the cutaneous metastatic sample demonstrated EGFR protein overexpression. Subsequent spatial analysis demonstrated that EGFR-high tumor regions strongly correlated with hyper-proliferative Ki67+ tumor cells. Furthermore, this EGFR-high niche was spatially associated with an immunosuppressive microenvironment characterized by the infiltration of PD-L1+ myeloid cells, CD14+ monocytes, regulatory T cells (Tregs), and PD-L1+/IDO1+ tumor cells. Therefore, we formulated a spatial profiling-guided therapeutic hypothesis and added gefitinib to the prior regimen of lenvatinib plus tislelizumab concurrent with radiotherapy, achieving significant tumor regression despite subsequent intracranial progression. In conclusion, these findings suggest that spatial profiling offers valuable therapeutic insights, highlighting the potential benefit of an EGFR-targeted triplet strategy in refractory HCC with EGFR protein overexpression. While confounding effects from concurrent therapies cannot be excluded, this profiling-guided hypothesis warrants further prospective clinical and mechanistic validation.

articles.title: Glass versus resin microspheres in ⁹⁰Y radioembolization for hepatocellular carcinoma: toxicity patterns under uniform voxel-based dosimetry.
articles.authors: Ali Dablan, Enes Mustafa Kaya, Meryem Kaya, Emrah Birol, Çağrı Erdim, Mustafa Fatih Arslan, Mehmet Cingöz, Oğuzhan Türksayar
articles.abstract: To compare safety outcomes and toxicity patterns of glass and resin microspheres in patients undergoing yttrium-90 (⁹⁰Y) transarterial radioembolization (TARE) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), using uniform voxel-based dosimetry for both platforms and toxicity comparisons adjusted for treatment extent and tumor burden. This retrospective single-center study included 103 consecutive patients with HCC and preserved liver function treated with ⁹⁰Y-TARE between June 2020 and June 2024 using glass-based (n = 70) or resin-based (n = 33) microspheres, selected according to routine practice and product availability. Absorbed doses for both cohorts were derived from voxel-based ⁹⁹ᵐTc-MAA SPECT/CT dosimetry. Adverse events (AEs) were graded with CTCAE version 5.0. The primary endpoint was overall AE incidence; secondary endpoints were specific toxicity patterns and dose-toxicity associations, examined with multivariable logistic regression adjusting for treatment extent and tumor volume. Progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were compared with the log-rank test. Overall AE incidence did not differ between glass and resin microspheres (glass 37.1% vs. resin 30.3%; p = 0.497), and all AEs were grade 1-2. Tumor and non-tumorous liver absorbed doses were similar. Bilirubin toxicity was more frequent with glass microspheres (glass 28.6% vs. resin 9.1%; p = 0.027), whereas hemoglobin decline was more common with resin microspheres (glass 10.0% vs. resin 30.3%; p = 0.010); both exploratory differences persisted after adjustment for treatment extent and tumor volume. Lung shunt fraction, a baseline patient-level parameter, was higher with resin (glass 2.6% vs. resin 4.1%; p = 0.043). Higher lung absorbed dose was associated with AE occurrence overall, without a significant lung dose × microsphere-type interaction (p = 0.41). Neither PFS (median, glass 9 vs. resin 12 months; p = 0.868) nor OS (glass 23 vs. resin 29 months; p = 0.929) differed significantly. Glass and resin microspheres showed no significant difference in overall AE incidence-without formally establishing equivalence-but differed in their patterns of mild laboratory toxicity independently of treatment extent and tumor burden. These exploratory findings support careful, individualized dosimetric assessment and require confirmation in prospective multicenter studies, but do not provide criteria for microsphere selection.
