articles.title: Predictive value of genetic and morphological evaluation (GAME) score for outcomes after thermal ablation in patients with colorectal liver metastases.
articles.authors: Yaqing Kong, Xiaoning Yue, Xiaojing Cao, Fan Tang, Xiang Zhou
articles.journal: International journal of hyperthermia : the official journal of European Society for Hyperthermic Oncology, North American Hyperthermia Group
articles.abstract: To evaluate the predictive value of the genetic and morphological evaluation (GAME) score for the prognosis of patients with colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) receiving thermal ablation (TA) and compare it with the Fong score. We conducted a retrospective analysis of CRLM patients who underwent TA between January 2016 and December 2021 at two tertiary medical centers in China. Recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank testing. Prognostic variables associated with early recurrence (ER) and OS were identified through univariate and multivariate Cox regression, and nomograms were developed based on significant factors. Both the GAME and Fong scores effectively predicted RFS and OS in patients with CRLM undergoing TA treatment, though the GAME score showed superior discriminatory ability. Cox regression identified the largest liver metastasis diameter (HR: 0.45, 95% CI: 0.29-0.69; p < 0.001) and GAME group (HR: 1.88, 95% CI: 1.13-3.12; p = 0.015) as independent prognostic factors for ER. The largest liver metastasis diameter (HR: 0.49, 95% CI: 0.31-0.78; p = 0.003), image-guidance technique (HR: 2.10, 95% CI: 1.04-4.27; p = 0.039) and GAME group (HR: 1.88, 95% CI: 1.12-3.16; p = 0.017) were independent prognostic factors for OS. Based on these findings, nomograms with good discrimination and calibration were constructed. The GAME score, which outperforms the Fong score in predicting the prognosis of patients with CRLM who meet the stringent eligibility criteria of this study and undergo TA, should be considered a preoperative prognostic tool.

articles.title: Associations between tissue stiffness, tumor response to transarterial chemoembolization and prognosis in hepatocellular carcinoma: insights from multifrequency 3D-magnetic resonance elastography.
articles.authors: Jie Chen, Zhen Zhang, Zheng Ye, Yali Qu, Liping Deng, Yuan Yuan, Guoyong Chen, Hehan Tang
articles.abstract: To investigate the correlation between tissue stiffness, as measured across various target tissues using multifrequency three-dimensional magnetic resonance elastography (3D-MRE), and tumor responses to transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), as well as post-treatment prognosis in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). HCC patients scheduled for TACE treatment were prospectively recruited and received multifrequency 3D-MRE before the initiation of TACE procedure. Measurements of tumor stiffness (TS), liver stiffness (LS), and spleen stiffness (SS) were conducted at frequencies of 60 Hz and 30 Hz, respectively. Treatment response was assessed using the mRECIST. Patient follow-up was conducted to evaluate overall survival outcomes. The final patient cohort consisted of 43 patients (mean age: 56.66±10.13 years; 34 males), including 16 non-responders and 27 responders. Non-responders exhibited significantly elevated TS (4.10±2.54 vs. 2.68±1.61kPa, p=0.035), LS (2.88±1.43 vs. 1.97±0.59kPa, p=0.026), and SS (4.03±0.90 vs. 3.13±1.08kPa, p=0.008) at the frequency of 30Hz. Firth's penalized univariable logistic analysis identified age (adjusted odds ratio [OR]=0.93, P=0.036), tumor number (OR=0.69, P=0.035), LS at 60Hz (OR=0.79, p=0.046), TS at 30Hz (OR=0.73, p=0.037), LS at 30Hz (OR=0.44, p=0.008), and SS at 30Hz (OR=0.44, P=0.009) as potential predictors of treatment response. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for predicting treatment response was 0.69 for age, tumor number and TS at 30Hz, 0.67 for LS at both 60Hz and 30Hz, and 0.75 for SS at 30Hz. Univariable Cox regression identified TS at both 60Hz (hazard ratio=1.15, p=0.014) and 30Hz (hazard ratio=1.40, p=0.010) as potential predictors of overall survival. Spleen stiffness measured at 30 Hz via 3D-MRE may serve as a potential predictor of treatment response to TACE in HCC patients, whereas tumor stiffness measured at both 60Hz and 30Hz appears to correlate with overall survival. Further research is necessary to validate these preliminary associations.

articles.title: Early Prognostic Value of the Freiburg Index of Post-Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt Survival in Patients With Hepatocellular Carcinoma Undergoing Liver Transplantation.
articles.authors: Yifan Ling, Jiaxin Zhao, Mengni Jing, Yujiang Pang, Jie Zhou, Zhenhua Hu
articles.abstract: The Freiburg Index of Post-Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt (TIPS) Survival (FIPS) integrates clinically relevant indicators of hepatic and renal function, but its prognostic value in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) undergoing liver transplantation (LT) remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association of pre-transplant FIPS with post-transplant overall survival (OS) and HCC recurrence and to compare its prognostic performance with that of the Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD). Adult liver transplant recipients with HCC registered in the Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients (SRTR) between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2018, were included. Overall survival was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression. Because FIPS did not satisfy the proportional hazards assumption, interval-specific effects were estimated for 0-1, 1-2, and 2-3 years after transplantation. Parallel FIPS- and MELD-based prognostic models were compared using Harrell's C-index, time-dependent area under the curve (AUC), calibration analysis, decision-curve analysis, and five-fold cross-validation. HCC recurrence was evaluated using Fine-Gray competing-risk regression, with death without recurrence treated as a competing event. Patients with high FIPS had consistently lower post-transplant survival than those with low FIPS, with one-, two-, and three-year overall survival rates of 89.5%, 84.7%, and 79.6% versus 93.1%, 88.3%, and 83.8%, respectively. After multivariable adjustment, each one-unit increase in FIPS was significantly associated with higher mortality during the first year after transplantation (hazard ratio (HR): 1.125; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.069-1.183; P<0.001) and during years 2-3 (HR: 1.112; 95% CI: 1.040-1.190; P=0.002), demonstrating a time-dependent prognostic association. A sensitivity analysis excluding Milan criteria included 13,940 recipients and yielded directionally consistent associations, with significant estimates across all three follow-up intervals. FIPS-based risk prediction showed performance comparable to that of MELD across cross-validated C-index, time-dependent AUC, calibration, and decision-curve analyses. In competing-risk analysis, high FIPS showed a trend toward a higher risk of HCC recurrence (subdistribution hazard ratio (sHR): 1.22; 95% CI: 0.97-1.54; P=0.095). Pre-transplant FIPS captures time-dependent variation in early post-transplant survival among patients with HCC and provides prognostic information comparable to MELD. These findings support the potential use of FIPS as a complementary marker for pre-transplant risk stratification and early post-transplant prognostic assessment. Its relationship with post-transplant HCC recurrence warrants further investigation.

articles.title: On the role of high-lying correlated triplet pair states for singlet fission in TIPS-pentacene.
articles.authors: Alejandro Zepeda Herrera, Bartosz Błasiak, Reed Nieman, John B Asbury, Hans Lischka, Irene Burghardt
articles.abstract: Electronic structure calculations at the combined density functional theory and multi-reference configuration interaction (DFT/MRCI) level of theory are reported for dimer and trimer pentacene complexes representative of 6,13-bis(triisopropylsilylethynyl)pentacene (TIPS-pentacene) in a brickwork polymorph. In addition to the low-lying correlated triplet pair (CTP) states, high-energetic CTP states are reported which lie above the bright exciton state and feature non-negligible oscillator strength. Using a vibronic coupling Hamiltonian in conjunction with multiconfigurational quantum dynamical calculations, it is shown that despite the ultrafast decay towards the low-lying CTP manifold, these high-lying CTP states exhibit residual occupancies on a picosecond time scale. These findings support the interpretation given in [Grieco et al., J. Phys. Chem. C 2018, 122, 2012] regarding both prompt and persistent mid-IR absorption features following transient absorption of the bright exciton in crystalline TIPS-pentacene films.

articles.title: Quantifying the Role of Interventional Radiology in Managing Patients with Hepatobiliary Cancers.
articles.authors: Nishita Kothary, C Matthew Hawkins, Ashley Maleki, Wafa Q Khan, Danny R Hughes
articles.journal: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
articles.abstract: To quantify the role of interventional radiology (IR) in managing primary and secondary hepatobiliary cancers. This retrospective study analyzed administrative data from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) using final action claims for Medicare Fee-for-Service beneficiaries from 2016 to 2021. Patients aged ≥65 years with hepatobiliary cancer were identified using International Classification of Diseases (ICD), 10th Revision, codes. Services and associated work Relative Value Units (wRVUs) provided by IR, medical oncology, radiation oncology, and surgical oncology were identified using CMS physician specialty codes. IR procedures were classified as therapeutic or supportive. From 2016 to 2021, the Medicare hepatobiliary cancer cohort included 108,317-111,761 patients annually (mean age, 75 years; male, 53%). Medical oncologists treated 70% of patients, followed by interventional radiologists with 51%, radiation oncologists with 13%, and surgical oncologists with 5%. Physician service volumes and wRVU remained stable, with medical oncologists providing the largest share (69% of services and 13.7% of wRVUs), followed by interventional radiologists (2.9% and 11.7%, respectively), radiation oncologists (1.3% and 4.5%, respectively), and surgical oncologists (0.1% and 2.2%, respectively). Interventional radiologists performed 75,785 therapeutic procedures, primarily for hepatocellular carcinoma (59%). Before pandemic, IR volumes increased 57%, driven by liver ablations (+25%) and supportive services (+63%), whereas transarterial therapies declined slightly (-6%). Despite the drop in volume during the pandemic, IR saw the highest compound annual growth rate (4%) among the specialties analyzed. IR provides a substantial share of services for patients with hepatobiliary cancers, with rising use of therapeutic and supportive services, delivering similar wRVUs at lower costs, underscoring its growing role in cancer care.

articles.title: Drug Delivery Systems for Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Bridging Pathophysiological Barriers and Advanced Nanomedicine Strategies.
articles.authors: Guiwen Liang, Chuli Zhu, Hualin Sun, Jiahuan Gong, Yanan Ji, Lei Qi
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by high heterogeneity, a complex tumor microenvironment, and multiple physiological barriers that limit conventional therapies and cause significant toxicity. Drug delivery systems (DDS), particularly nanoscale delivery systems, offer promising opportunities to overcome these obstacles through passive targeting, active targeting, and stimuli-responsive drug release. Nevertheless, despite substantial progress in preclinical research, the clinical translation of most DDS remains challenging. This review systematically outlines the pathophysiological rationale underpinning DDS design for HCC, including the aberrant vasculature, hypoxia, low pH, overexpressed enzymes and immunosuppressive features of the TME, as well as liver-specific barriers. Subsequently, we comprehensively evaluate the progress and limitations of passive targeting, active targeting, stimuli-responsive, and locoregional delivery systems. Furthermore, we dissect the core bottlenecks currently impeding clinical translation: tumor heterogeneity, the "interlocking chain" effect of multiple biological barriers, uncertainty of the EPR effect, multidrug resistance mechanisms, poorly defined long-term safety of nanocarriers, and the "valley of death" caused by discrepancies between preclinical models and human disease. Finally, we envision future directions: next-generation targeting strategies should focus on CSCs and metastasis; DDS must be deeply integrated with immunotherapy to remodel the immune microenvironment; biomimetic and bio-derived delivery systems may circumvent inherent limitations of synthetic carriers; multifunctional theranostic platforms enable real-time monitoring and personalized treatment; and establishing more clinically relevant animal models alongside personalized DDS design paradigms is key to accelerating translation. Our central argument is that the future success of DDS for HCC will no longer rely on the "showmanship" of individual technologies, but rather on a "systems engineering" approach grounded in a profound understanding of HCC biological heterogeneity, with the core objectives being precise spatiotemporal control of drug distribution and beneficial interactions with the host immune system.

articles.title: Transarterial Radioembolization in the Treatment of Hepatocellular Carcinoma and Combination Strategies.
articles.authors: P Pantelis, C Damaskos, N Garmpis, G Tsourouflis, D Dimitroulis
articles.abstract: This review provides a comprehensive overview of transarterial radioembolization (TARE) using Yttrium-90 (Y-90), a minimally invasive locoregional therapy for HCC patients who are ineligible for surgical resection. A narrative review of the literature was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus databases. Studies focusing on patient selection, technical aspects, dosimetry, safety, oncologic outcomes and combination strategies were included. Clinical guidelines, prospective and retrospective studies, and comparative analyses were synthesized. A total of 43 key publications were synthesized, including landmark randomized controlled trials (SARAH, SIRveNIB, DOSISPHERE-01), recent meta-analyses and current clinical practice guidelines from EASL, AASLD and ESMO. Transarterial radioembolization demonstrates high objective response rates and favorable survival outcomes across Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) stages, with a favorable safety profile compared to systemic therapies. Personalized dosimetry approaches significantly improve response rates as demonstrated in the DOSISPHERE-01 trial. Combination strategies with immune checkpoint inhibitors and tyrosine kinase inhibitors show promising synergistic potential, supported by ongoing phase II/III trials including IMMUWIN, ROWAN and EMERALD-Y90. Transarterial radioembolization is a safe and effective locoregional therapy for HCC, with expanding indications including radiation segmentectomy with curative intent, downstaging for transplantation and combination with systemic therapies. Future research should focus on optimal sequencing, personalized dosimetry thresholds and identification of patients who are most likely to benefit from combination approaches.

articles.title: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Atrial Fibrillation Recurrence After Catheter Ablation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Panagiotis Theofilis, Paschalis Karakasis, Panayotis K Vlachakis, Konstantinos Pamporis, Aikaterini Vordoni, Evangelos Oikonomou, Kyriakos Dimitriadis, Gerasimos Siasos
articles.abstract: Catheter ablation (CA) is an established rhythm-control strategy for atrial fibrillation (AF); however, AF recurrence remains common and is influenced by the underlying cardiometabolic substrate, including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). This study aimed to evaluate the association of MASLD and MASLD-related fibrosis risk with AF recurrence following CA. We conducted a systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of observational studies reporting AF recurrence after CA, stratified by MASLD status and liver fibrosis risk, as assessed using the fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index and the non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) fibrosis score (NFS). Eligible studies included adults undergoing CA for AF with recurrence outcomes reported and stratified by MASLD or fibrosis risk categories. A total of 160 records were identified, and seven studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Six studies, including 2921 patients, contributed to the primary meta-analysis comparing MASLD versus no MASLD. An additional fibrosis-only study contributed to fibrosis-stratified analyses. The meta-analysis of six studies (MASLD: 894; non-MASLD: 2027) demonstrated that MASLD was associated with a significantly higher risk of AF recurrence after CA (risk ratio (RR) 1.77, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.43-2.18; p < 0.001; I2 = 64.1%). In a separate meta-analysis of five studies reporting adjusted estimates, MASLD remained significantly associated with recurrence (hazard ratio (HR) 2.13, 95% CI 1.49-3.04; p < 0.001; I2 = 70.5%). In fibrosis-stratified analyses, Intermediate/High FIB-4 (RR 2.03, 95% CI 1.27-3.26; p = 0.003; I2 = 71.3%) and Intermediate/High NFS (RR 1.65, 95% CI 1.12-2.43; p = 0.01; I2 = 49.9%) were associated with a higher risk of AF recurrence compared with low scores. MASLD is associated with a significantly higher risk of AF recurrence after CA. Fibrosis risk stratification using FIB-4 and NFS also shows a significant association between Intermediate/High fibrosis and increased recurrence rates. articles.title: Hepatocellular- cholangiocarcinoma collision tumor: a case report.
articles.authors: Hongzhi Cao, Lin Long, Canbin Xie, Yu Liu, Jianqi Zou, Lin Sun
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma collision tumor is an extremely rare primary liver malignancy, defined as histologically distinct hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) growing adjacently with clear demarcation, which is easily misdiagnosed due to overlapping features with combined hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma and metastatic liver cancer, and lacks standardized diagnostic and treatment evidence. We report a 54-year-old male with 15-year chronic hepatitis B infection admitted in June 2024 with fatigue, poor appetite and abdominal distension. Preoperative CT initially suggested multifocal metastatic HCC, while Gd-EOB-DTPA MRI indicated dual primary tumors, and multi-target biopsy confirmed HCC-ICC collision tumor (S8 segment grade III HCC, S6 segment moderately differentiated ICC, no mixed components). After multidisciplinary team (MDT: Oncology Department, Interventional Vascular Surgery Department, Hepatobiliary Surgery Department, Radiology Department, Internal Medicine for Liver Diseases Department, Infectious Diseases Department) discussion, the patient was ineligible for surgery due to lymph node metastases, received transarterial chemoembolization for the HCC lesion, followed by sequential PD-1 inhibitor(Sintilimab) plus bevacizumab and 8 cycles of gemcitabine plus cisplatin. As of the last follow-up on April 20, 2026, the patient had an overall survival of over 18 months with partial response lesions and no severe adverse events. This case indicates that HCC-ICC collision tumor should be considered in the differential diagnosis of multifocal liver malignancies, multi-target biopsy is critical for accurate diagnosis, and individualized combination therapy targeting both components can achieve favorable survival outcomes, adding to the clinical evidence for this rare disease.

articles.title: Hepatic retromer is essential for systemic cholesterol homeostasis by regulating lysosomal cholesterol handling.
articles.authors: Cristy R C Verzijl, Markus G Barbosa, Dyonne Y Vos, Andries H Heida, Amandine Caillaud, Lauri Vanharanta, Xiaoke Ge, Joël J Tissink
articles.abstract: Disturbed hepatic cholesterol homeostasis is associated with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). The endo-lysosomal system plays a central role in cholesterol uptake and intracellular trafficking, yet the molecular mechanisms governing these processes remain poorly understood. Here, we identify hepatic vacuolar protein sorting 35 (VPS35), a core component of the retromer complex, as a critical regulator of hepatocellular and systemic cholesterol homeostasis. Liver-specific VPS35 ablation in mice elevated plasma and hepatic cholesterol levels due to impaired hepatic uptake of atherogenic lipoproteins, defective cholesterol trafficking through the endo-lysosomal system, and increased de novo cholesterol biosynthesis. The decreased hepatic uptake of atherogenic lipoproteins was associated with altered subcellular distribution of the low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR) and reduced levels of LDLR-related protein 1 (LRP1). The increased hepatic cholesterol content was associated with altered lysosomal ultrastructure and pH and decreased levels of a wide range of lysosomal proteins, including key proteins for lysosomal cholesterol egress, such as lysosomal acid lipase (LAL), scavenger receptor class B member 2 (SCARB2), Niemann-Pick type C1 (NPC1), and NPC2. Collectively, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized function of the hepatic retromer complex in systemic cholesterol homeostasis. Beyond its established role in endosomal cargo transport, VPS35 is essential for lysosomal cholesterol handling by preserving key proteins involved in lysosomal cholesterol metabolism.

articles.title: Preparation and evaluation of degradable imaging drug loaded embolization microspheres for hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.authors: Qi Lai, Ye Fan, Junyi Huang, Ling Huang, Huade Zheng
articles.journal: Journal of biomaterials science. Polymer edition
articles.abstract: Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) necessitates the use of embolic agents with intrinsic radiopacity and controlled biodegradability to enhance therapeutic precision. In addressing the limitations inherent in current drug-eluting microspheres (DEMs), this study introduces the development of inherently radiopaque and biodegradable (DOX+Lipiodol) @PLGA @CaCO3 @Alg core-shell microspheres. These microspheres were synthesized using rotating membrane emulsification and surface-induced ion crosslinking, with calcium carbonate serving multiple roles: a solid surfactant for Pickering stabilization, an acid-neutralizing agent, and an alginate shell inducer. The microspheres successfully encapsulated iodine loads, demonstrated by CT values reaching up to 8,000 HU, and contained doxorubicin at 1.53 ± 0.12 wt.%. They exhibited prolonged radiopacity for over 14 days in vivo and showed a pH-responsive drug release pattern, releasing 90% of their payload at pH 5.2 compared to 30% at pH 7.2 over 120 h. The sequential degradation process (alginate → CaCO3 → PLGA) resulted in greater than 60% mass loss within four months, correlating with a reduction in CT attenuation. In rabbit embolization models, the microspheres achieved effective vascular occlusion and induced ischemic necrosis in ears and kidneys. CT tracking was possible without additional contrast agents, and systemic biosafety was confirmed with cell viability exceeding 90%, hemolysis below 1%, and normal hematological and histological profiles. These findings suggest that the microspheres could serve as a clinically translatable platform for image-guided TACE, integrating occlusion, therapy, and monitoring into a cohesive treatment strategy.

articles.title: Functional validation and characterization of Slc39a8 genotype effects on ethanol consumption and related phenotypes.
articles.authors: André Lucas Silva-Borges, Donna-Jael G Paredes, Rebeka Sultana, Cecilia G Pareja, Amanda M Barkley-Levenson
articles.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
articles.abstract: Alcohol use disorders are heritable, and large-scale genome-wide association studies have recently identified novel genetic loci that are correlated with alcohol consumption and problematic alcohol use. One such gene is Slc39a8 , which encodes the ion transporter ZIP8, responsible for cellular import of zinc and other metals. Slc39a8 is highly pleiotropic, and a common missense variant has been associated with decreased problematic alcohol use. Here, we used Slc39a8 heterozygous (HET) knockout mice and their wild type (WT) littermates to characterize the effects of reduced gene function on two models of voluntary alcohol consumption (drinking in the dark and intermittent access two-bottle choice), and anxiety- and depression-like behavior. We found that HET mice consumed less alcohol than WT in the intermittent access two-bottle choice procedure. No evidence was found for genotypic differences in baseline locomotor activity, anxiety-like, or depression-like behavior in the open field and forced swim tests. Slc39a8 mRNA expression and alcohol metabolism experiments confirmed decreased brain expression of Slc39a8 in HET mice and unchanged alcohol metabolism. Basal and post-alcohol measurement of zinc levels showed that HET mice after ethanol exposure had lower zinc concentrations in the liver and higher concentrations in blood than WT animals. Analysis of the spatial distribution of multiple trace metals in the brains of naïve Slc39a8 HET and WT mice using Laser Ablation Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (LA-ICP-MS) showed region-specific genotypic differences in levels of zinc and iron. These results provide evidence for a direct role of Slc39a8 in ethanol consummatory behavior that does not appear to be due to metabolism, affective state, or locomotor activity. Moreover, we confirm that this animal model shows tissue- and brain region-specific alterations in zinc levels, highlighting potential mechanisms for future study.

articles.title: Preoperative depressive symptoms as an independent prognostic factor for long-term survival after curative-intent treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma: a prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Xingyu Mi, Guo Long, Yilin Pan, Kui Chen, Shiqi Lu, Yifan Man, Liang Xiao, Jianing Tang
articles.abstract: Depression is common in cancer patients and may affect prognosis, yet its impact on long-term outcomes after curative-intent treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is underexplored. We prospectively examined whether preoperative depressive symptoms (Zung Self-Rating Depression Scale score ≥ 53) independently predict poorer overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) in HCC patients undergoing curative-intent treatment. A total of 213 pathologically confirmed HCC patients who underwent resection or ablation at Xiangya Hospital (2019) were enrolled. Depressive status was assessed by the Zung Self-Rating Depression Scale (cutoff≥53), dividing patients into screen-positive (n = 66) and screen-negative (n = 147) groups. The primary endpoint was OS; the secondary endpoint was DFS. Follow-up ended December 2025. Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses adjusted for demographic, clinical, pathological, and treatment covariates. The screen-positive group included more females (21.2% vs. 10.9%, P = 0.05) and more patients with low educational attainment (69.7% vs. 52.4%, P = 0.04), whereas partner status and alcohol use were balanced. Median follow-up was 77 months. Depressive symptoms significantly worsened DFS (median 12.0 vs. 24.0 months; HR = 1.42, P = 0.02) and OS (median 41.0 vs. 55.0 months; HR = 1.78, P < 0.001). Multivariable Cox analysis confirmed depressive symptoms as an independent adverse factor for both DFS (HR = 1.45, 95% CI: 1.04-2.01, P = 0.03) and OS (HR = 1.50, 95% CI: 1.05-2.14, P = 0.03). The DFS model adjusted for age, partner status, BCLC stage, AFP, type of surgery, MVI, and Ki-67; the OS model additionally adjusted for educational attainment and alcohol use status. Preoperative depressive symptoms independently predict shorter DFS and OS after curative-intent treatment for HCC. Routine screening for depressive symptoms may help identify patients at higher risk; whether psychosocial intervention improves long-term outcomes requires further study.

articles.title: Effective treatment of orthotopic liver cancer with bifunctional embolization microspheres.
articles.authors: Baoqu Zhang, Jianke Li, Jianmin Zhao, Yanwu Peng, Perumal Ramesh Kannan, Han Zhang, Xiangdong Kong, Rui Tang
articles.abstract: Transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE) is a minimally invasive procedure used widely for the treatment of unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, embolization-induced hypoxia upregulates VEGF, and the resulting angiogenic response contributes to tumor recurrence, further limiting the efficacy of TACE against HCC. Herein, we present a multifunctional embolic microsphere system in which sorafenib (SRF) and calcium carbonate (CaCO3) nanoparticles are rationally encapsulated within sodium hyaluronate microspheres (SRF-CaCO3@SH MSs) via microfluidic technology. The microspheres exhibited a bowl-shaped morphology with tunable diameters, which enhances in vivo embolic stability through mechanical interlocking between adjacent microspheres. In an acidic tumor microenvironment (TME), pH-triggered release of Ca²⁺ (23.9%) and SRF (65.7%) far exceeded neutral conditions. SRF-CaCO3@SH MSs maintained >85% HUVEC viability and reduced VX2 cell viability to 24.3%, showing maximal cytotoxicity under acidic conditions. After intra-arterial injection, the microspheres occluded tumor-feeding arteries; Ca²⁺ released in the acidic TME inhibited angiogenesis, and CaCO3 neutralized TME acidity, counteracting immunosuppression. In a rabbit VX2 orthotopic HCC model, DSA-guided TACE achieved effective occlusion, slowest tumor growth, largest necrosis, and marked downregulation of CD31, Ki67, and VEGF, without systemic toxicity. Combining morphological design, pH-responsive occlusion, TME neutralization, and anti-angiogenesis, this embolic system synergistically enhances TACE and shows strong clinical potential. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Conventional liver cancer embolization frequently fails due to hypoxia-driven angiogenesis and subsequent tumor recurrence. We developed a dual-functional embolic microsphere (SRF-CaCO3@SH MS) that integrates stable vascular occlusion with active modulation of the tumor microenvironment. Utilizing microfluidics, we fabricated bowl-shaped sodium hyaluronate microspheres that mechanically interlock to ensure durable embolization. Under acidic tumor conditions, calcium carbonate neutralizes pH and releases Ca²⁺, which synergizes with sorafenib to inhibit angiogenesis and induce apoptosis. In a rabbit orthotopic HCC model, this system demonstrated superior tumor control and necrosis without inducing systemic toxicity. This work presents a microenvironment-responsive embolization strategy integrating durable vascular occlusion, pH modulation, and anti-angiogenic therapy.

articles.title: Global deletion of the triglyceride-synthesizing enzyme TMEM68 disrupts hepatic lipid homeostasis in mice.
articles.authors: Haonan Wang, Huimin Pang, Christoph Heier, Chunyan Zhang, Tingting Li, Yuhang Liu, Feifei Huang, Pingan Chang
articles.abstract: Transmembrane protein 68 (TMEM68) mediates triacylglycerol (TAG) synthesis in mammals independently of canonical diacylglycerol acyltransferase (DGAT) 1 and DGAT2 enzymes. However, the in vivo roles of TMEM68 including its contribution to tissue-specific TAG formation remain largely elusive. In this study, we used a global Tmem68 knockout mouse model to investigate the impact of TMEM68 deficiency on lipid and energy metabolism of the liver. We found that loss of TMEM68 leads to a transient reduction in hepatic TAG storage and circulating ketone bodies approximately 4 weeks after birth. TMEM68-deficient livers exhibited reduced abundance of distinct acylglycerols and fatty acids, altered glycerophospholipid composition, and accumulation of polar ether lipids. Primary TMEM68-deficient hepatocytes also had reduced TAG and lipid droplet contents. RNA sequencing revealed that genes involved in multiple fatty acid metabolic processes and ketogenesis were repressed in Tmem68 knockout livers. Furthermore, Tmem68 ablation reduced hepatic cholesterol esters and modulated bile acid composition. In summary, our study identifies TMEM68 as a positive regulator of hepatic storage lipid levels and demonstrates a multifaceted embedding of the enzyme in hepatic lipid and energy metabolic pathways.

articles.title: Artificial Induction of Mitochondrial Calcification as a Trigger for Cancer Immunotherapy.
articles.authors: Kaixin Zhang, Hanhui Li, Zhuoxin Wang, Hongkun Wu, Li Shi, Qingqing Feng, Hongye Guan, Ben Wang
articles.abstract: Tumor calcification shows promise as a clinical predictor of tumor response and often involves mitochondrial calcification, which provides mineral precursors for extracellular deposition. However, the methods available for regulating mitochondrial calcification in tumor calcification therapy are limited. Herein, we designed and synthesized (4-carboxybutyl) triphenylphosphonium bromide (CTPP)-functionalized calcium peroxide (CaO2) nanoparticles (CTPP/CaO2) to achieve selective induction of mitochondrial calcification in hepatocellular carcinoma cells. The CTPP/CaO2-induced mitochondrial calcification sustains elevated intracellular calcium ion (Ca2+) and reactive oxygen species (ROS), exacerbates mitochondrial dysfunction, and triggers tumor cell death via pyroptosis. Pyroptosis further promotes the release of intracellular contents and exposure of calreticulin on the cell membrane, effectively activating the antitumor immune response in vivo. This mitochondrial calcification strategy integrates direct killing of tumor cells with subsequent activation of the antitumor immune response, thus providing a promising approach for engineering mitochondrial calcification with potential applications in cancer therapy. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Tumor calcification is a promising anticancer therapeutic strategy, but most existing methodologies are confined to non-specific extracellular mineralization with unsatisfactory targeting precision. We herein report a mitochondria-targeted nanoplatform that selectively initiates mitochondrial calcification against hepatocellular carcinoma. The resultant mitochondrial impairment and persistent ROS overproduction drive tumor pyroptosis, enabling direct tumor ablation and robust antitumor immune activation. Meanwhile, in situ tumor calcification augments CT/MR imaging contrast. This mitochondria-targeted calcification strategy achieves integrated theranostics and provides a potential strategy for refractory solid malignancies.

articles.title: Vulnerability and Immunogenic Cell Death under Microwave Ablation for Synergistic Treatment of Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
articles.authors: Zide Chen, Hongwei Xu, Yufu Peng, Mengni Zhu, Linqing Huang, Feng Fang, Kefei Chen
articles.abstract: Microwave ablation (MWA) holds great promise for hepatocellular carcinoma but is often limited by incomplete tumor eradication and recurrence. Here, we report a tumor-killing nanoimmunoreactor driven by endogenous immune cues that synergizes with MWA to eliminate residual tumors and activate systemic antitumor immunity. The 17-AAG-MnO2PEG nanoimmunoreactor consists of a self-responsive PEGylated MnO2 platform loaded with the HSP90 inhibitor 17-allylamino-17-demethoxygeldanamycin (17-AAG), which is designed to respond to the oxidative tumor microenvironment. 17-AAG disrupts tumor cell thermotolerance, enhancing sensitivity to microwave-induced thermal stress, thereby improving ablation efficacy and inducing immunogenic cell death. PEGylation facilitates tumor-targeted accumulation, while the degradable MnO2 responds to hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) and tumor debris generated after MWA, enabling sustained local drug release. The combination treatment promotes dendritic cell maturation and T cell infiltration, effectively suppresses residual tumor regrowth, reduces the risk of metastasis, and establishes durable immune memory. By leveraging post-ablation tumor debris and microenvironmental cues, this strategy couples local tumor ablation with systemic antitumor immunity, providing a mechanistically distinct paradigm for durable cancer therapy.

articles.title: Same-Day Radioembolization for Large Hepatocellular Carcinoma (≥ 5 cm) Using Yttrium-90 Resin Microspheres: Protocol for a Multicenter Prospective Registry Study (ISTAR-01).
articles.authors: Hyo-Cheol Kim, In Joon Lee, Dongho Hyun, Gyoung Min Kim
articles.abstract: This study aims to evaluate the technical feasibility of same-day yttrium-90 (Y-90) radioembolization in patients with large hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) (≥ 5 cm) who are predicted to have a low lung shunt fraction (LSF) based on imaging features. This prospective, multicenter, open-label, single-arm registry study will enroll patients with large HCC without imaging features suggestive of high LSF. Eligible patients will undergo same-day planning angiography, technetium-99 m macroaggregated albumin (99mTc-MAA) scintigraphy, and Y-90 radioembolization using resin microspheres. Key eligibility criteria include tumor size ≥ 5 cm, Child-Pugh class A liver function, and absence of imaging findings associated with elevated LSF. Imaging indicators of high LSF include hepatic vein invasion, early hepatic vein enhancement, transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt, and dysmorphic intratumoral vessels ≥ 3 mm. The primary endpoint is the proportion of patients successfully undergoing same-day treatment among those scheduled. Secondary endpoints include objective response rate (ORR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and treatment-related toxicity. A total of 139 patients will be enrolled to estimate feasibility, assuming a success rate of 90% with a 5% margin of error at a 95% confidence level. ORR will be compared using the chi-square test, while PFS and OS will be evaluated using the Kaplan-Meier method and compared using the log-rank test. This study will provide prospective evidence regarding the feasibility and clinical outcomes of same-day radioembolization in large HCC. NCT06944483.

articles.title: Phase IIa Trial of Locoregional High-Dose Autologous Natural Killer Cell Therapy Combined with Hepatic Arterial Infusion Chemotherapy for Locally Advanced Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
articles.authors: Hyeon-Jong Kim, Yang Seok Koh, Byung Chan Lee, Yang-Hyun Baek, Jung Gil Park, Jeong Won Jang, Hyung-Seok Kim, Je-Jung Lee
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) refractory to locoregional therapies remains a major clinical challenge. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of locoregional high-dose autologous natural killer (NK) cell therapy combined with hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC) in patients with locally advanced HCC. This open-label, multicenter, phase IIa study enrolled patients with locally advanced HCC refractory to standard care. Patients achieving stable disease (SD) or better after two HAIC cycles (5-fluorouracil and cisplatin) underwent two additional HAIC cycles followed by hepatic arterial NK cell infusion for up to two cycles. The primary endpoint was independent review committee (IRC)-assessed objective response rate (ORR). Secondary endpoints included investigator-assessed ORR, disease control rate (DCR), duration of response (DOR), time to progression (TTP), overall survival (OS), safety, and immunologic response. Tumor response was assessed per modified RECIST for HCC. Of 17 enrolled patients, 16 were evaluable. IRC-assessed ORR was 68.75% (exact 95% confidence interval, 41.34-88.98) [complete response (CR): 18.75%; partial response (PR): 50.00%], and investigator-assessed ORR was 62.50%. Both assessments yielded a DCR of 100%. Median DOR was 12.65 and 10.48 months by IRC and investigator assessment, respectively. Median investigator-assessed TTP was 16.82 months; IRC-assessed TTP was not reached. Median OS was 24.05 months. No severe NK cell-related toxicities were observed. Locoregional high-dose autologous NK cell therapy following HAIC showed promising antitumor activity and an acceptable profile in selected patients with locally advanced HCC. These findings warrant validation in randomized trials designed to isolate the incremental contribution of NK cell therapy.

articles.title: Reirradiation using brachytherapy for locally recurrent soft tissue sarcoma: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Ashwin Subramaniam, William Jin, Benjamin Rich, Brooke Crawford, Francis Hornicek, Julie Grossman, Emily Jonczak, Jonathan Trent
articles.abstract: Managing locally recurrent soft tissue sarcomas (STS) following prior radiation therapy remains challenging due to the lack of retreatment options and heightened risk of treatment-associated toxicity. Brachytherapy enables delivery of highly localized radiation with rapid dose fall-off and may serve to address these types of tumors. This systematic review evaluates the efficacy and safety of brachytherapy in the management of locally recurrent STS. A systematic review was conducted, and its findings are reported in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. PubMed was searched through July 9, 2026, using Medical Subject Heading (MeSH) terms related to recurrent sarcoma, brachytherapy, and reirradiation. Studies were included if they reported local control and/or toxicity outcomes following brachytherapy-based treatment for locally recurrent STS. Case reports, case series with fewer than 5 patients, studies with significant institutional overlap, and studies evaluating retroperitoneal disease were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data on local control, survival outcomes, and treatment-related toxicity. Seven retrospective studies met inclusion criteria. Five-year local control rates ranged from 18% to 87%, with better outcomes generally associated with multimodality therapy, smaller tumor burden, and fewer prior recurrences. Overall survival varied across cohorts and was influenced by factors such as tumor grade, recurrence burden, surgical margins, and prior radiation exposure. Grade 3-4 complication rates ranged from 0% to 49%, with higher rates observed in reirradiation settings and cumulative radiation doses approaching or exceeding 100-110 Gy. Emerging approaches, including stereotactic ablative brachytherapy and template-guided placement, demonstrated favorable early safety profiles. Brachytherapy represents a viable salvage strategy for selected patients with locally recurrent STS; however, outcomes remain heterogeneous. Prospective, multi-institutional studies with standardized reporting are needed to better define its role in the re-irradiation setting.

articles.title: Beyond Tumor Treating Fields: Multimodal Antitumor Action and the Clinical Potential of Pulsed Electromagnetic Fields.
articles.authors: Qian-Wen Zeng, Ming-Jie Liu, Li-Sha Yi, Shuang Wu, Pei-Pei Zhu, Hong-Zhi Hu, Zheng-Qi Shao
articles.abstract: Pulsed electromagnetic fields (PEMFs) are a noninvasive, safe, and well-tolerated physical therapy modality with established applications in musculoskeletal disorders. Their potential role in oncology has attracted increasing interest. This review synthesizes current evidence on the antitumor mechanisms and experimental effects of PEMFs across diverse cancer models. Reported biological effects include the induction of apoptosis, regulation of intracellular calcium homeostasis, inhibition of angiogenesis, modulation of immune responses, induction of oxidative stress, regulation of autophagy and cellular metabolism, and enhancement of sensitivity to radiotherapy and chemotherapy. Preclinical studies suggest that PEMFs can selectively suppress proliferation and promote cell death in malignant cells while exerting comparatively limited cytotoxicity in normal cells. Evidence has been reported in models of breast cancer, glioma, hepatocellular carcinoma, melanoma, and other malignancies. Although clinical investigations remain preliminary, studies conducted over the past two decades support a favorable safety profile and suggest potential therapeutic efficacy, particularly in combination with chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or immunotherapy. Artificial intelligence and machine learning may facilitate parameter optimization and the development of individualized treatment regimens. Ultimately, the integration of PEMFs into routine oncology practice will require well-designed, large-scale randomized controlled trials to standardize treatment protocols, define clinical indications, and establish their role in multimodal cancer care.

articles.title: Outcomes of Elderly Patients with Colorectal Liver Metastases Treated with Liver-Directed Therapies.
articles.authors: Nafeesah Fatimah, Morgan F Pettigrew, Victoria F Peters, Christine F Johansen, Matthew R Porembka, Alex C Kim, John C Mansour, Adam C Yopp
articles.abstract: Liver-directed therapy (LDT) is an essential component of multimodal management of colorectal liver metastases (CRLM), yet older adults are less likely to receive liver-directed or curative-intent treatment. We evaluated presentation, treatment patterns, and outcomes among elderly patients with CRLM. We retrospectively reviewed patients with CRLM treated at the University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center and Parkland Memorial Hospital from 2016 to 2023. Liver-directed therapy was defined as liver resection, hepatic artery infusion pump therapy, ablation, liver-directed radiation including external beam radiation and stereotactic body radiation, transarterial chemoembolization, and/or Y-90 radioembolization. The primary outcome was overall survival (OS); the secondary outcome was receipt of LDT. Cox proportional hazards regression identified factors associated with OS among patients aged ≥70 years. Among 852 patients, 710 were aged <70 years and 142 were aged ≥70 years. Liver metastasis number, bilobar involvement, CEA level, and extrahepatic disease were similar between age groups. Older adults were less likely to receive LDT than younger patients (20% vs. 40%, p < 0.001). Among patients who underwent hepatic resection, perioperative outcomes were similar by age. Among older adults, LDT was associated with longer median OS than no LDT (44 vs. 9 months, p < 0.001). Among patients receiving LDT, median OS was comparable between age groups (44 vs. 52 months, p = 0.19). Performance status, CEA ≥200 ng/mL, chemotherapy, and LDT were independently associated with OS. Older adults with CRLM were less likely to receive LDT. Among selected older adults, receipt of LDT was associated with longer OS than no LDT. Chronological age alone should not preclude consideration of LDT.

articles.title: Transarterial Radioembolization Versus Chemoembolization for Unresectable Large Single Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
articles.authors: Myungsu Lee, Minuk Kim, Jayoun Kim, Do Hoon Kim, Jin Wook Chung, Hyo-Cheol Kim
articles.abstract: To compare oncologic outcomes and safety between transarterial radioembolization (TARE) and transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) in patients with unresectable large solitary hepatocellular carcinomas (HCCs; ≥6 cm). This single-center retrospective study included patients with a solitary HCC ≥6 cm who underwent initial treatment with TARE or TACE between January 2010 and December 2023. Patients who were initially scheduled to undergo TARE but were subsequently treated with TACE because of a high lung shunt fraction (LSF) were included in the TACE group. The primary outcome was overall survival (OS), and secondary outcomes included progression-free survival (PFS), local PFS, tumor response, and safety. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was used to adjust for baseline differences in the survival analyses. In total, 306 patients were included in this study (TACE, n = 187; TARE, n = 119). Before IPTW adjustment, the TARE group demonstrated significantly longer OS than the TACE group (median, 79.6 vs. 46.5 months; P = 0.004). Patients who were ineligible for TARE because of extensive lung shunting demonstrated particularly poor survival (median OS, 20.3 months). After IPTW adjustment, TARE remained associated with longer OS (median, 79.6 vs. 53.4 months; P = 0.033) and local PFS (median, 25.1 vs. 9.5 months; P = 0.001). Median PFS remained numerically longer with TARE (9.8 vs. 7.8 months), but the difference did not reach statistical significance (P = 0.066). In comparison with TACE, TARE was associated with less frequent serious adverse events (10.1% vs. 26.7%; P < 0.01) and a markedly lower rate of prolonged hospitalization (>7 days) (0.8% vs. 22.5%; P < 0.01). In patients with unresectable large solitary HCCs, TARE was associated with longer OS, improved local tumor control, and fewer serious adverse events than TACE. However, the survival advantage should be interpreted with caution, because biological selection related to LSF eligibility may have contributed to the observed difference.

articles.title: Safety and early outcomes of external beam radiation therapy with low dose brachytherapy boost in patients with prostate cancer: A single institution experience.
articles.authors: Zakaria El Kouzi, Michael K Rooney, Adam B Samman, Ramez Kouzy, Seungtaek Choi, Henry Mok, Karen Hoffman, Quynh-Nhu Nguyen
articles.abstract: To evaluate the safety and early oncologic outcomes of external beam radiation therapy (EBRT) combined with a low-dose-rate (LDR) brachytherapy boost in patients with intermediate- and high-risk prostate cancer, as contemporary real-world evidence remains limited. Investigators retrospectively reviewed 307 patients treated at a large tertiary cancer center between 1999 and 2024. Median age was 66 years; 36% had intermediate-risk and 64% had high- or very high-risk disease, and 91% received androgen deprivation therapy. Late gastrointestinal (GI) and genitourinary (GU) toxicities were defined as occurring more than three months after radiation initiation and graded using CTCAE version 5. Biochemical failure was defined using Phoenix criteria. Outcomes were summarized descriptively; Cox regression analyzed overall survival (OS) and biochemical recurrence-free survival (bRFS), while Fine-Gray models evaluated late toxicity with death as a competing risk. At a median follow-up of 4.6 years, 22 patients developed biochemical recurrence. Five-year bRFS was 98% for intermediate-risk disease and 90% for high- or very high-risk disease; OS and bRFS were 92% and 95%, respectively. Grade 3 or higher GU and GI toxicity occurred in 3.2%, and no significant predictors of severe late toxicity were identified. These findings support this approach for appropriately selected patients in routine clinical care.

articles.title: Regional Expansion of Transplant Oncology: The First Case of Liver Transplantation for Unresectable Colorectal Liver Metastasis in the Gulf Region.
articles.authors: Fatima AlKhyeli, Juan S Barajas-Gamboa, Chase J Wehrle, Essa Aleassa, Mahmoud Nalawi, Omar Abu Sham, Sandra El Hajj, Ahmad Raza
articles.abstract: Liver transplantation for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) has emerged as a potential curative option for highly selected patients with unresectable liver-only disease, with recent trials demonstrating 5-year overall survival rates of 55% to 83%. Surgical resection remains the only curative treatment for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM), but its applicability is limited, with only 25% of patients eligible. However, this approach remains investigational with limited global experience and has never been implemented in the Middle East region. Recently, liver transplantation (LT) has emerged as a potential curative option for select patients with unresectable liver-only metastases. This report highlights the potential for liver transplantation to serve as a curative modality in highly selected patients with CRLM and demonstrates its feasibility in a new geographic region. We report the first case in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region of a 41-year-old male with unresectable CRLM who underwent LT following an aggressive multimodal pretransplant protocol. The patient was initially treated at an outside facility for synchronous left-sided colorectal cancer with liver metastases, achieving complete remission after FOLFOX chemotherapy. He subsequently developed 2 liver recurrences: the first in July 2023, with 17 metastases managed at the outside facility by surgical resection and chemotherapy; and the second in October 2023, with 40 metastases, treated with systemic chemotherapy and trans arterial radioembolization (TARE-Y90). He received additional treatment with ablative liver-directed therapies consistent with the "Cleveland Protocol." The patient subsequently underwent orthotopic liver transplantation. His postoperative course was complicated with moderate acute cellular rejection, which was successfully treated, and he was discharged on post-operative day 16. This case demonstrates the successful implementation of liver transplantation for CRLM in the Gulf region, achieving disease-free survival at 4-month follow-up despite high-risk biological features typically associated with poor prognosis. It illustrates the feasibility and potential benefit of LT for unresectable CRLM in carefully selected patients, following an aggressive pretransplant locoregional therapy protocol modeled after the Cleveland Clinic approach. Key success factors included rigorous patient selection using established criteria (Oslo score 0, low Fong score, low PET-MTV), intensive pretransplant optimization with multimodal therapy, and experienced multidisciplinary management of post-transplant complications. With careful patient selection and integration of systemic and liver-directed therapies to achieve maximal disease control, this strategy may help expand transplant eligibility, possibly offering a curative approach. This case provides valuable regional data for the evolving role of transplant oncology in colorectal cancer management in a resource-limited setting.

articles.title: Characterization of Bubble Cloud Formation and Tissue Ablation Using a High-Frequency Endoscopic Histotripsy System.
articles.authors: Victor A Lopez, Jessica Gannon, Amber Keith, Tamalika Paul, Thomas G Landry, Jeffrey K Woodacre, Jeremy A Brown, Irving C Allen
articles.abstract: Histotripsy is a non-thermal focused ultrasound (US) ablation strategy that non-invasively destroys tissue by generating a cavitation bubble cloud. Prior work has established the potential of histotripsy for many applications, including the non-invasive treatment of liver tumors. To expand histotripsy beyond the currently available clinical systems for targeting deep abdominal tumors, recent work has developed miniaturized high-frequency devices capable of greater precision using devices within an endoscopic form factor. This work investigates the use of one of these high-frequency histotripsy devices to evaluate cavitation generation and ablation capacity in a variety of ex vivo porcine tissues (brain, liver, kidney, pancreas and lymph node) and in vivo murine liver. A 6.3 MHz histotripsy transducer with an aperture of 10 mm and a focal length of 7 mm was co-registered with a 30 MHz US imaging array. Optical imaging was used to identify the cloud formations for different pulsing cycles, while US imaging was used to monitor ex vivo and in vivo histotripsy ablations in tissue. Histological sections were examined, and statistical analyses were performed on imaging data. Well-defined bubble clouds ranging from 0.54 ± 0.12 mm to 0.82 ± 0.12 mm (axial) were maintained over the course of 10,000 pulses for 3, 5, 8 and 12 cycles for peak negative pressures (p-) of 33-42 MPa. Larger bubble clouds were generated at a higher p- for all cycles. Pearson correlation coefficients of >0.8 for all cases indicated a strong correlation between US and optical imaging. Histotripsy bubble clouds were identified and maintained on US imaging with hypoechoic zones seen immediately post treatment for all tissue types in both ex vivo and in vivo treatments. Histological results showed complete ablation of the targeted regions in excised porcine brain, kidney, pancreas and lymph nodes. Ex vivo porcine liver exhibited extensive loss of hepatocytes but did retain subtle lobular architecture due to remnants of portal connective tissue. In vivo murine liver showed partial ablation, suggesting that higher treatment doses are required. These results demonstrate the potential of miniaturized high-frequency histotripsy devices for precise and effective histotripsy ablation across a wide range of potential applications and establish the potential of this device for use in preclinical murine histotripsy studies.

articles.title: Procedural Micro-Costing of Single-Room Transcatheter CT Hepatic Angiography for Microwave Liver Ablation.
articles.authors: Emma C Dunne, Mengjun Wu, Regina Navato, Jakob Mathiszig-Lee, Nicos Fotiadis, Edward W Johnston
articles.abstract: To quantify the resource use and procedural costs attributable to transcatheter CT hepatic angiography during single-room computed tomography-guided microwave ablation of liver tumours. A prospective bottom-up micro-costing analysis was conducted from the UK National Health Service perspective. Resource utilisation data were collected from 35 consecutive patients undergoing hepatic angiography-assisted microwave ablation in a single-room equipped with a standard computed tomography scanner and a mobile C-arm. Unit costs were identified using National Health Service reference costs and the Personal Social Services Research Unit databases. Per-procedure costs incorporated staff time, equipment and consumables, and imaging-related capital costs. Median costs were £4,499 (£2,361-8,001) for the ablation component and £1,142 (£929-1,584) for hepatic angiography, with a median combined procedure cost, calculated independently, of £5,689 (£3,533-9,296). The hepatic angiography component was equivalent to 25.4% of the median ablation-component cost. Among the sensitivity scenarios tested, angiography duration had the greatest influence on its incremental cost, producing estimates of £929-1,584. Hepatic angiography adds a measurable incremental cost to computed tomography-guided microwave ablation. These results provide a foundation for prospective studies evaluating whether improved intraprocedural assessment translates into reduced re-intervention and improved cost-effectiveness. Level 4, case series.

articles.title: Unlocking Prognostic Potential: Serum Uric Acid and Prothrombin Time as Predictors of HCC Recurrence.
articles.authors: Yanping Xiao, Qing Lin, Kunrong Yang, Guangjian Su
articles.abstract: This study aims to explore the prognostic value of pre-treatment serum uric acid (UA) and prothrombin time (PT) levels on the risk of tumor recurrence in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) after receiving comprehensive therapy. A total of 199 HCC patients who underwent combination therapy (including surgical resection, local ablation, interventional therapy, and systemic therapy) at Fujian Cancer Hospital from January 2020 to December 2022 were consecutively enrolled. Baseline clinical data and pre-treatment laboratory indicators were collected. The primary endpoint was recurrence-free survival (RFS), with a median follow-up time of 19 months. The optimal cutoff values for UA and PT of predicting recurrence were determined using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Independent risk factors affecting RFS were analyzed using the Cox proportional hazards regression model. The Kaplan-Meier method was used to plot survival curves to compare differences between groups and to construct nomograms. Spearman's correlation analysis was also conducted. A total of 116 patients (58.3%) experienced recurrence. Multivariate Cox regression analysis showed that UA (HR = 1.486, 95% CI: 1.009 - 2.189, p = 0.045) and PT (HR = 1.510, 95% CI: 1.011 - 2.261, p = 0.046) were independent risk factors for HCC recurrence. Furthermore, based on optimal cutoff values determined by ROC curve analysis, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis confirmed that recurrence-free survival (RFS) was significantly lower in the low-UA group and short-PT group (p < 0.05). Correlation analysis indicated that UA and PT had no significant correlation with alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), a traditional tumor marker for HCC, with p > 0.05, suggesting that their prognostic information is independent of traditional tumor markers. Elevated pre-treatment serum uric acid (UA) levels and prolonged prothrombin time (PT) are independent predictive factors for recurrence after combined therapy in HCC patients. These two indicators, as routine and easily accessible clinical tests, are cost-effective and have significant potential for application in improving postoperative risk stratification, identifying high-risk patient groups, and guiding individualized follow-up strategies for HCC patients.

articles.title: Portosystemic Anastomoses: A Narrative Review of Anatomy, Clinical Significance of Spontaneous Portosystemic Shunts, and Contemporary Therapeutic Approaches.
articles.authors: Angelos Ntalaoutis, Theodore Troupis, Dimosthenis Chrysikos, Dimitrios Filippou
articles.abstract: Portosystemic anastomoses represent natural or acquired vascular communications between the portal venous system and the systemic circulation, which under physiological conditions constitute vessels of minimal flow and no clinical significance, yet become dilated and develop in states of portal hypertension, predominantly in the context of liver cirrhosis. This narrative review aims to elucidate the complex and essentially dual role of these anastomoses, with particular focus on the spontaneous portosystemic shunts (SPSS) that develop in cirrhotic patients, their clinical significance, and the contemporary therapeutic approaches developed for their management. A systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Google Scholar (from September 2025 to July 2026), without language restrictions, using MeSH terms and free-text keywords including "portosystemic anastomoses," "spontaneous portosystemic shunts," "portal hypertension," "hepatic encephalopathy," "TIPS," and "BRTO." A structured search strategy was applied, incorporating Boolean operators (AND/OR). No formal quantitative synthesis (meta-analysis) was performed. This is a narrative review synthesising published findings from eligible studies. A total of 847 initial records were identified, 644 were screened after duplicate removal, 123 were assessed for full-text eligibility, and 46 studies were ultimately included. The synthesis of the literature reveals that portosystemic anastomoses are anatomically classified into oesophagogastric, anorectal, paraumbilical, and retroperitoneal types, with the spontaneous splenorenal shunt (SSRS) representing the most commonly identified large SPSS in advanced cirrhosis. The presence of SPSS, particularly when their total shunt area (TSA) exceeds 83 mm², is independently associated with an increased risk of hepatic encephalopathy (HE) and mortality, regardless of the Child-Pugh or Model for End-stage Liver Disease (MELD) score. The relationship between SPSS and variceal bleeding is complex and counterintuitive, as the presence of SPSS does not appear to confer protection against haemorrhagic events. Therapeutic management relies primarily on the transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) and on selective embolisation techniques, including balloon-occluded retrograde transvenous obliteration (BRTO), plug-assisted retrograde transvenous obliteration (PARTO), and coil-assisted retrograde transvenous obliteration (CARTO), while surgical shunts retain a role in selected patient categories. This review concludes that portosystemic anastomoses are not a neutral imaging finding but an active participant in the natural course of cirrhosis, with an initially compensatory yet ultimately detrimental character. Their recognition, quantification, and individualised management are critical parameters in the contemporary clinical approach to the patient with cirrhosis and portal hypertension.

articles.title: Preoperative radioembolization versus chemoembolization and upfront resection for resectable hepatocellular carcinoma beyond the Milan criteria.
articles.authors: Jeayeon Park, Gyung Sun Lim, Yunmi Ko, Hyunjae Shin, Moon Haeng Hur, Su Young Hong, Suk Kyun Hong, Yun Bin Lee
articles.abstract: As the role of transarterial radioembolization (TARE) in resectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) beyond Milan criteria remains undefined, this study compared preoperative TARE and chemoembolization (TACE) with primary resection to establish the optimal management strategy. We retrospectively analyzed HCC patients who did not meet the Milan criteria and underwent primary liver resection, preoperative TACE, or preoperative TARE. Overall survival (OS), time to recurrence (TTR), and recurrence-free survival (RFS) were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and Cox regression with inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). A total of 226 patients were included (primary resection, n = 127; preoperative TACE, n = 52; preoperative TARE, n = 47), with a median follow-up of 37.2 months. After IPTW, baseline characteristics were well balanced. Median OS was not reached in the primary resection and preoperative TARE, but was 60.7 months in the preoperative TACE group. Compared with primary resection, preoperative TACE was associated with worse OS (adjusted HR [aHR]: 2.72; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.39-5.33; p = 0.004), whereas OS with preoperative TARE was comparable (aHR: 1.14; 95% CI: 0.50-2.55; p = 0.76) after IPTW. Similarly, TTR and RFS were significantly worse in the preoperative TACE (both p = 0.02), whereas no significant differences were observed between the preoperative TARE and primary liver resection groups after IPTW (p = 0.59 and p = 0.57). Preoperative TARE showed no significant difference in survival from primary liver resection in resectable HCC beyond the Milan criteria and may serve as a reasonable alternative strategy when upfront surgery is not feasible. Question Optimal treatment for resectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) beyond the Milan criteria is controversial. The role of preoperative transarterial radioembolization (TARE) compared with chemoembolization (TACE) or upfront resection remains unclear. Findings Preoperative TARE achieved survival outcomes comparable to primary resection, whereas preoperative TACE was associated with significantly inferior overall and recurrence-free survival. Clinical relevance Preoperative TARE demonstrates survival outcomes comparable to primary resection. It serves as a reasonable therapeutic alternative for resectable hepatocellular carcinoma beyond the Milan criteria, offering effective local control when immediate surgery is not feasible.

articles.title: Immunotherapy and targeted therapy plus hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy for HCC with portal vein tumor thrombosis (CHANCE2504): a nationwide target trial emulation study.
articles.authors: Long-Wang Lin, Qian Chen, Jia-Wei Zhou, Zhen Li, Bin Xiong, Jian-Song Ji, Xiao-Li Zhu, Bin-Yan Zhong
articles.abstract: The treatment strategy for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with portal vein tumor thrombosis (PVTT) remains controversial because of its the dismal prognosis. This study aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) plus molecular-targeted agents (MTA) with or without hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC) as a first-line treatment for HCC with PVTT. This nationwide retrospective cohort study utilized a target trial emulation framework with a clone-censor-weighting (CCW) approach and was conducted in 36 centers across China. The study population comprised patients diagnosed with HCC and PVTT who received HAIC in combination with ICIs and MTA (HAIC-ICIs-MTA) or ICIs plus MTA (ICIs-MTA) from June 2018 to December 2024. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS), which was evaluated through restricted mean survival time (RMST) with bootstrapping. Secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS), objective response rate (ORR), and safety profiles. This study included a total of 1649 HCC patients (614 in the HAIC-ICIs-MTA group and 1035 in the ICIs-MTA group). After CCW, the median OS of the HAIC-ICIs-MTA group was 23.3 months, whereas that of the ICIs-MTA group was 16.4 months. The difference in RMST for OS was 7.4 months (95% confidence interval [CI]: 3.5-11.7, bootstrapped P<0.001). The HAIC-ICIs-MTA group also had a significantly longer median PFS (8.7 months vs. 6.2 months, bootstrapped P=0.002) with an RMST of 2.6 months (95% CI: 0.9-4.5), and a higher ORR (38.9% vs. 22.7%, P<0.001) as per the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors Version 1.1. Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 243 patients in the HAIC-ICIs-MTA group (39.6%) and 335 patients in the ICIs-MTA group (32.4%). HAIC in combination with ICIs and MTA is associated with improved survival and an acceptable safety profile compared to ICIs plus MTA alone, supporting this regimen as a promising treatment strategy for HCC patients with PVTT that warrants further prospective validation.

articles.title: A novel clinical FIT model predicts prognosis of unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma treated with TACE combined with lenvatinib and PD-1 inhibitors therapy.
articles.authors: Minjun Liao, Zilong Wang, Xiaoxiao Wang, Xin Ai, Linnan Song, Yuyun Song, Wanying Qin, Kai Wang
articles.abstract: Transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE) with lenvatinib and programmed death-1 (PD-1) inhibitors therapy (triple therapy) demonstrated encouraging efficacy for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC). This study developed and validated a novel prognostic model to evaluate prognosis of uHCC patients with triple therapy, and identify patients who may benefit from triple therapy. uHCC patients receiving triple therapy were retrospectively enrolled from multiple centers. Overall survival (OS) was the primary endpoint. The prognostic model was developed based on multivariate Cox regression derived predictors of OS. Prognosis was evaluated by Kaplan-Meier survival curves. 265 uHCC patients were enrolled (training cohort: n = 160; validation cohort: n = 105). The objective response and disease control rate were 52.5 and 77.7%, respectively. The optimal cut-off point for fibrin degradation products (FDP) and serum iron level were determined as 4.7 μg/dL and 60.0 μg/dL, respectively. Multivariate Cox regression identified FDP, serum iron level and tumor burden score (TBS) as independent predictors of OS, and these clinical parameters established the FIT model. The FIT model demonstrated favorable discriminative capability for predicting OS with AUC of 0.809 (95% CI: 0.740-0.879) and 0.798 (95% CI: 0.710-0.886) in the training and validation cohorts, respectively. Kaplan-Meier analyses revealed significant prognostic stratification for OS and progression-free survival (PFS) among risk groups defined by FIT model (p < 0.001). Subgroup analyses in alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), tumor number and Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) stage subsets confirmed the prognostic relevance of FIT model in uHCC. The novel clinical FIT model could effectively predict survival of uHCC patients receiving triple therapy, and facilitate prognostic stratification.

articles.title: FZD7 Shapes Mitochondrial Function and Oxidative Stress in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Potential Prognostic Biomarker.
articles.authors: Peishu Huang, Fuqun Wei, Yiping Chen, Yuanmeng Yang
articles.abstract: Mitochondrial metabolism and oxidative stress (OS) play critical roles in the progression of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, reliable prognostic biomarkers for these processes remain unidentified. This study integrated bulk RNA sequencing and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to identify OS&mitochondrial metabolism-related genes (OMRGs). A prognostic model was constructed using LASSO regression, followed by external validation. Associations of the model with clinicopathological features, tumor microenvironment (TME), immune functions, therapeutic response, and drug sensitivity were systematically explored. Finally, the relationships between key OMRGs and mitochondrial metabolism as well as OS were validated. A risk score based on five key OMRGs (LPCAT1, IMPDH1, RAMP3, FZD7, and B4GALT5) was established. Low OMRS was significantly associated with improved overall survival and identified as an independent prognostic factor. Two subtypes (C1/C2) were characterized based on the OMRGs: the C1 subtype exhibited poorer survival and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) enrichment, whereas the C2 subtype showed greater immune infiltration and sensitivity to immunotherapy. High OMRS was associated with higher predicted IC50 values to oxaliplatin and cisplatin, while low OMRS indicated favorable responses to TACE, sorafenib, and immunotherapy. FZD7 knockdown increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels and reduced mitochondrial membrane potential in HCC cells. FZD7, a key gene among OMRGs, represent promising prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets in HCC.

articles.title: Efficacy of In-Office Bleaching Using 35% Hydrogen Peroxide in an Attachable Syringe Varying the Application Tip: A Double-Blind Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.authors: Gabrielle Gomes Centenaro, Laryssa Mylenna Madruga Barbosa, Leticia Condolo, Marina Kravchychyn Cappelletti, Alessandro D Loguercio
articles.journal: Journal of esthetic and restorative dentistry : official publication of the American Academy of Esthetic Dentistry ... [et al.]
articles.abstract: This randomized clinical trial evaluated the bleaching efficacy (BE), absolute risk and intensity of tooth sensitivity (TS), gingival irritation (GI), and esthetic self-perception (ES) of an in-office bleaching gel with an attachable syringe using different application tips in a randomized, double-blind (participant- and evaluator-blinded) clinical trial. Forty-five participants received hemi-arch bleaching using an attached brush and a conventional tip, performed in two sessions with hydrogen peroxide 35%. BE was evaluated at baseline, weekly, and 1-month post-bleaching using a spectrophotometer (ΔEab, ΔE00, and ΔWID) and shade guide units (ΔSGU). The absolute risk and intensity of TS and GI using a VAS. ES was assessed using the Orofacial Esthetic Scale. BE was analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVA. TS and GI were evaluated using the McNemar test (absolute risk) or paired t-test (intensity and ES scores; α = 0.05). BE was observed for both groups, with no statistical difference (p > 0.05) across all parameters. The absolute and intensity of TS were comparable between brush and conventional tip (p > 0.05). ES was improved after bleaching (p < 0.05). The application tips showed equivalent bleaching efficacy and esthetic self-perception, as well as similar tooth sensitivity and gingival irritation. The brush applicator tip preserved bleaching efficacy while minimizing the volume of gel applied to the tooth surface, making it a more sustainable alternative.

articles.title: Ex Vivo Comparative Experiments Demonstrating the Ablation Effect of a Temperature-Controlled Radiofrequency Ablation System.
articles.authors: Kenjiro Yamamoto, Takao Itoi, Yuki Joyama, Takayoshi Tsuchiya, Ryosuke Tonozuka, Shuntaro Mukai, Kazumasa Nagai, Hiroyuki Kojima
articles.abstract: A temperature-controlled radiofrequency ablation (TC-RFA) system has been introduced to reduce excessive thermal damage and enable safer treatment. However, the ablation effect of this system remains to be fully elucidated. Therefore, this ex vivo study aimed to directly compare the ablation characteristics of the TC-RFA with those of a power-controlled RFA (PC-RFA). Pig liver specimens were used. The TC-RFA using all four probe types and the PC-RFA were performed step-by-step to macroscopically evaluate the ablation area and speed. Linear regression models with interaction terms were used to compare changes in ablation dimensions over time between RFA devices and probes. The TC-RFA produced different short-axis ablation diameters depending on the probe even at the same temperature setting and generated an ablation effect at an earlier time, with substantially less change in ablation dimensions over time than the PC-RFA. In contrast, the PC-RFA had the slowest onset, but its ablation area continued to increase in width and depth with longer ablation durations. These differences in ablation behavior over time were statistically significant (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). In these exploratory ex vivo experiments, the TC-RFA system produced earlier and more consistent ablation effects over time than the PC-RFA system.

articles.title: Perfusion beyond Margin in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Contrast-enhanced US Feature Related to Tumor Invasiveness and Prognosis.
articles.authors: Wenzhen Ding, Ran Ji, Chuan Pang, Jianming Li, Fangyi Liu, Jie Yu, Ping Liang
articles.abstract: Background Previous studies on imaging of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) have shown inconsistency in the growth of tumor vascularity and gross morphologic features. Contrast-enhanced US (CEUS) is one of the few methods that can depict both features simultaneously, making it valuable for assessing this inconsistency and its potential clinical influence. Purpose To evaluate and establish a new CEUS feature representing inconsistency between vascularity and gross morphologic features (perfusion beyond margin [PBM]) and analyze its underlying biologic mechanisms and prognostic influence. Materials and Methods This multicenter retrospective study included patients with HCC from January 2015 to August 2023. Three radiologists (5-8 years of experience) measured tumor diameter using gray-scale US and CEUS. Mathematic, prognostic, and bioinformatics analyses were used to quantify the PBM diagnostic standard. Prognostic analysis included recurrence-free survival after laparoscopic hepatectomy and local tumor progression-free survival after thermal ablation. Bioinformatics analysis included pathologic and immunohistochemical evaluation and RNA sequencing. Results This study included 1076 patients (mean age ± SD, 60 years ± 10.5; 854 men, 1166 HCCs). PBM was defined as the tumor diameter on arterial phase exceeding that at gray-scale US by 5 mm.
